sentences.zh: 建文元年，周、代、湘、齊、岷五王相繼以罪廢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwen, the five princes of Zhou, Dai, Xiang, Qi, and Min were successively degraded on charges of crime.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jianwen reign, the five princes of Zhou, Dai, Xiang, Qi, and Min were stripped of their titles one after another on criminal charges.

sentences.zh: 七月，燕王舉兵反，師名「靖難」。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the Prince of Yan raised troops in rebellion; the army was named "Pacifying Difficulties."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Prince of Yan rose in arms; his campaign was called "Pacifying the Difficulties."

sentences.zh: 指泰、子澄為奸臣。

translations.literal: He pointed to Tai and Zicheng as treacherous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He named Tai and Zicheng as traitorous ministers.

sentences.zh: 事聞，泰請削燕屬籍，聲罪致討。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Tai requested that Yan be struck from the clan register and that crimes be proclaimed to launch punitive action.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Tai urged that the Prince of Yan be removed from the imperial clan rolls and that formal charges be proclaimed to justify a punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 或難之，泰曰：「明其為賊，敵乃可克。」

translations.literal: Some objected; Tai said, "Make clear that he is a rebel, and only then can the enemy be overcome."
translations.idiomatic: Some raised objections, but Tai said, "Once he is plainly branded a rebel, the foe can be beaten."

sentences.zh: 遂定議伐燕，布告天下。

translations.literal: Thereupon the decision to campaign against Yan was settled and proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The court then resolved on war against Yan and issued the proclamation to the empire.

sentences.zh: 時太祖功臣存者甚少，乃拜長興侯耿炳文為大將軍，帥師分道北伐，至真定為燕所敗。

translations.literal: At that time very few of the founding emperor's meritorious ministers still survived; the court appointed Changxing Marquis Geng Bingwen Grand General, to lead armies north in several columns, but at Zhending he was defeated by Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Few of the founding emperor's great ministers still lived; the court therefore appointed Changxing Marquis Geng Bingwen grand general and sent him north at the head of several columns, only to be defeated by Yan forces at Zhending.

sentences.zh: 子澄薦曹國公李景隆代將，泰極言不可。

translations.literal: Zicheng recommended Duke of Cao Li Jinglong to replace him as commander; Tai spoke vehemently against it.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng recommended Duke of Cao Li Jinglong to take command in his place, but Tai argued fiercely against it.

sentences.zh: 子澄不聽，卒命景隆將。

translations.literal: Zicheng would not listen, and in the end Jinglong was appointed to command.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng would not heed him, and in the end Jinglong was put in command.

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝舉五十萬兵畀景隆，謂燕可旦夕滅。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor raised five hundred thousand troops and entrusted them to Jinglong, saying Yan could be destroyed within a day or two.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then committed five hundred thousand men to Jinglong, convinced that Yan could be wiped out within days.

sentences.zh: 燕王顧大喜曰：「昔漢高止能將十萬，景隆何才，其眾適足為吾資也！」

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan looked back and said in great joy, "In old times Emperor Gaozu of Han could command only one hundred thousand men—what talent has Jinglong? His multitude will do nicely as my supplies!"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan glanced back and exclaimed with delight, "Emperor Gaozu of Han could lead only a hundred thousand men at most—what ability has Jinglong? His host will serve nicely as my provisions!"

sentences.zh: 是冬，景隆果敗。

translations.literal: That winter, Jinglong was indeed defeated.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Jinglong was indeed routed.

sentences.zh: 帝有懼色，會燕王上書極詆泰、子澄。

translations.literal: The emperor showed fear; just then the Prince of Yan submitted a memorial violently denouncing Tai and Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fear showed on the emperor's face; at the same time the Prince of Yan sent up a memorial savagely denouncing Tai and Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 帝乃解二人任以謝燕，而陰留之京師，仍參密議。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon relieved the two of their offices to placate Yan, yet secretly kept them in the capital, still taking part in confidential deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then dismissed the two from office as a gesture to placate Yan, yet secretly kept them in the capital, where they still joined in confidential counsel.

sentences.zh: 景隆遺燕王書，言二人已竄，可息兵。

translations.literal: Jinglong sent the Prince of Yan a letter saying the two had already fled and that he could cease hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglong wrote to the Prince of Yan that the two had already fled and that he might stand down his arms.

sentences.zh: 燕王不聽。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan refused.

sentences.zh: 明年，盛庸捷東昌，帝告廟，命二人任職如故。

translations.literal: The next year Sheng Yong won a victory at Dongchang; the emperor reported to the ancestral temple and ordered the two restored to their posts as before.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Sheng Yong won a victory at Dongchang; the emperor reported to the ancestral temple and restored the two to their former offices.

sentences.zh: 及夾河之敗，復解二人官求罷兵，燕王曰：「此緩我也。」

translations.literal: When defeat came at Jiahe, the two were again dismissed from office in a request to halt the war; the Prince of Yan said, "This is to stall me."
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Jiahe the two were again removed from office in a bid to halt the war; the Prince of Yan said, "This is meant to stall me."

sentences.zh: 進益急。

translations.literal: His advance grew all the more pressing.
translations.idiomatic: His advance grew only more urgent.

sentences.zh: 始削藩議起，帝入泰、子澄言，謂以天下制一隅甚易。

translations.literal: When the plan to reduce the feudatories was first raised, the emperor took Tai and Zicheng's counsel and said that with the realm to control a single corner would be very easy.
translations.idiomatic: When the plan to pare back the princely domains was first broached, the emperor accepted Tai and Zicheng's advice and judged that with the whole realm in hand, controlling one corner would be easy.

sentences.zh: 及屢敗，意中悔，是以進退失據。

translations.literal: After repeated defeats he inwardly regretted it, and thus lost his footing in advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated defeats he came to regret it inwardly, and so lost his footing between pressing forward and pulling back.

sentences.zh: 迨燕兵日逼，復召泰還。

translations.literal: As Yan troops pressed daily closer, Tai was summoned back again.
translations.idiomatic: As Yan forces drew nearer day by day, Tai was summoned back once more.

sentences.zh: 未至，京師已不守，泰走外郡謀興復。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, the capital could no longer be held; Tai fled to outer prefectures to plot restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could arrive the capital was lost; Tai fled into the outer prefectures to plot restoration.

sentences.zh: 時購泰急。

translations.literal: At that time the price on Tai's head was urgent.
translations.idiomatic: A heavy price was then set on Tai's head.

sentences.zh: 泰墨白馬走，行稍遠，汗出墨脫。

translations.literal: Tai dyed a white horse black and fled; after he had gone some distance, sweat made the ink come off.
translations.idiomatic: Tai dyed a white horse black and fled; after he had ridden some distance, sweat washed the ink away.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「此齊尚書馬也。」

translations.literal: Someone said, "This is Grand Secretary Qi's horse."
translations.idiomatic: Someone cried, "That is Grand Secretary Qi's horse!"

sentences.zh: 遂被執赴京，同子澄、方孝孺不屈死。

translations.literal: He was thereupon seized and taken to the capital, and together with Zicheng and Fang Xiaoru died unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: He was seized and taken to the capital, where he died unbowed together with Zicheng and Fang Xiaoru.

sentences.zh: 泰從兄弟敬宗等皆坐死，叔時永、陽彥等謫戍。

translations.literal: Tai's cousins Jingzong and others were all condemned to death for association; his uncles Shiyong, Yangyan, and others were exiled to garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Tai's cousins Jingzong and the rest were all put to death by association; his uncles Shiyong, Yangyan, and others were banished to frontier garrison service.

sentences.zh: 子甫六歲，免死給配，仕宗時赦還。

translations.literal: His son Pu, six years old, was spared death and assigned in bonded service; during the reign of Emperor Shizong he was pardoned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pu, only six, was spared execution and assigned in penal service; under Emperor Shizong he was pardoned and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 黃子澄，名湜，以字行，分宜人。洪武十八年，會試第一。由編修進修撰，伴讀東宮，累遷太常寺卿。惠帝為皇太孫時，嘗坐東角門謂子澄曰：「諸王尊屬擁重兵，多不法，奈何？」對曰：「諸王護衛兵，才足自守。倘有變，臨以六師，其誰能支？漢七國非不強，卒底亡滅。大小強弱勢不同，而順逆之理異也。」太孫是其言。比即位，命子澄兼翰林學士，與齊泰同參國政。謂曰：「先生憶昔東角門之言乎？」子澄頓首曰：「不敢忘。」退而與泰謀，泰欲先圖燕。子澄曰：「不然，周、齊、湘、代、岷諸王，在先帝時，尚多不法，削之有名。今欲問罪，宜先周。周王，燕之母弟，削周是剪燕手足也。」謀定，明日入白帝。

translations.literal: Huang Zicheng, personal name Shi, was known by his style. He was from Fenyi. In Hongwu year eighteen he ranked first in the metropolitan examination. From compiler he advanced to revising editor, attended and read in the Eastern Palace, and was repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. When Emperor Hui was imperial grandson, he once sat at the East Corner Gate and said to Zicheng, "The princes are senior kinsmen and command heavy troops; many act unlawfully. What is to be done?" Zicheng replied, "The guards of the princes are barely enough for self-defense. If there is a change and the six armies are brought against them, who could withstand them? The seven kingdoms of Han were not weak, yet in the end they were destroyed. The circumstances of great and small, strong and weak are different, and the principles of obedience and rebellion are different." The imperial grandson approved his words. When he came to the throne, he ordered Zicheng also to serve as Hanlin Academician and to participate in state government with Qi Tai. He said, "Sir, do you remember the old words at the East Corner Gate?" Zicheng kowtowed and said, "I dare not forget." After withdrawing he planned with Tai, and Tai wanted first to plan against Yan. Zicheng said, "No. The princes of Zhou, Qi, Xiang, Dai, and Min were still often unlawful in the time of the former emperor, so there is a name by which to strip them. If we now wish to call someone to account, we should first take Zhou. The Prince of Zhou is Yan's full younger brother; stripping Zhou cuts off Yan's hands and feet." Once the plan was settled, the next day they entered and reported it to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zicheng, whose personal name was Shi and who was known by his style, came from Fenyi. In Hongwu 18 he placed first in the metropolitan examination. He rose from compiler to revising editor, served as companion reader in the Eastern Palace, and was eventually promoted to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. When Emperor Hui was still imperial grandson, he once sat at the East Corner Gate and asked Zicheng, "The princes are senior kinsmen and command large forces, and many of them violate the law. What should be done?" Zicheng replied, "Their princely guards are only enough for self-defense. If anything changes and the imperial armies are brought against them, who could resist? The seven kingdoms of Han were not weak, yet they were finally destroyed. Great and small, strong and weak differ in circumstance, and obedience and rebellion differ in principle." The imperial grandson approved. After taking the throne, he appointed Zicheng concurrently as Hanlin Academician and had him participate in affairs of state with Qi Tai. He asked, "Sir, do you remember what was said at the East Corner Gate?" Zicheng kowtowed and answered, "I dare not forget." After withdrawing, he planned with Tai. Tai wanted to move first against Yan, but Zicheng said, "No. The princes of Zhou, Qi, Xiang, Dai, and Min were already often lawless under the former emperor, so there is a proper charge for stripping them. If we are to call a prince to account, we should begin with Zhou. The Prince of Zhou is Yan's full younger brother; stripping Zhou is cutting off Yan's hands and feet." The plan settled, they entered the next day and reported it to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 會有言周王橚不法者，遂命李景隆帥兵襲執之，詞連湘、代諸府。

translations.literal: When someone reported that Prince Zhou Zhu Su had acted unlawfully, Li Jinglong was ordered to lead troops in a surprise arrest; the case implicated the households of Xiang, Dai, and others.
translations.idiomatic: When reports reached the court that Prince Zhou, Zhu Su, had broken the law, Li Jinglong was ordered to lead troops in a surprise arrest; the case implicated the households of Xiang, Dai, and other princes.

sentences.zh: 於是廢橚及岷王楩為庶人；

translations.literal: Thereupon Su and Prince Min Zhu Bian were degraded to commoners;
translations.idiomatic: Su and Prince Min, Zhu Bian, were thereupon reduced to commoner status;

sentences.zh: 幽代王桂於大同；

translations.literal: Prince Dai Zhu Gui was confined at Datong;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dai, Zhu Gui, was confined at Datong;

sentences.zh: 囚齊王榑於京師。

translations.literal: Prince Qi Zhu Fu was imprisoned in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qi, Zhu Fu, was imprisoned in the capital.

sentences.zh: 湘王柏自焚死。

translations.literal: Prince Xiang Zhu Bai burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiang, Zhu Bai, burned himself to death.

sentences.zh: 下燕議周王罪。

translations.literal: Yan was ordered to deliberate on Prince Zhou's crime.
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to Yan to deliberate Prince Zhou's offenses.

sentences.zh: 燕王上書申救，帝覽書惻然，謂事宜且止。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan submitted a memorial pleading for mercy; the emperor, reading it, was moved and said the matter should for the moment cease.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan memorialized in his defense; reading it, the emperor was moved and said the matter ought to rest for now.

sentences.zh: 子澄與泰爭之，未決，出相語曰：「今事勢如此，安可不斷？」

translations.literal: Zicheng and Tai disputed it without resolution; going out they said to each other, "The situation is as it is now—how can we not act decisively?"
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng and Tai argued the point to no conclusion; leaving the audience they said to one another, "Matters stand as they do—how can we fail to act decisively?"

sentences.zh: 明日又入言曰：「今所慮者獨燕王耳，宜因其稱病襲之。」

translations.literal: The next day they entered again and said, "What alone concerns us now is the Prince of Yan; we ought to strike while he claims illness."
translations.idiomatic: The next day they entered again and said, "Our sole concern now is the Prince of Yan; we should strike while he claims to be ill."

sentences.zh: 帝猶豫曰：「朕即位未久，連黜諸王，若又削燕，何以自解於天下？」

translations.literal: The emperor hesitated and said, "I have not long been on the throne; having dismissed prince after prince, if I now reduce Yan as well, how am I to justify myself to the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated. "I have not long been enthroned," he said. "Having already demoted prince after prince, if I now move against Yan as well, how can I justify myself to the empire?"

sentences.zh: 子澄對曰：「先人者制人，毋為人制。」

translations.literal: Zicheng replied, "He who acts first controls others; do not let others control you."
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng answered, "He who strikes first controls others; do not let others control you."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「燕王智勇，善用兵。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The Prince of Yan is wise and brave and skilled in employing troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Prince of Yan is wise and brave and skilled at war.

sentences.zh: 雖病，恐猝難圖。」

translations.literal: Even if ill, I fear he would be hard to take by surprise."
translations.idiomatic: Even if he is ill, I fear a sudden strike would be hard to carry off."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The plan was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 於是命都督宋忠調緣邊官軍屯開平，選燕府護衛精壯隸忠麾下，召護衛胡騎指揮關童等入京，以弱燕。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor ordered Regional Commander Song Zhong to shift frontier garrison troops to camp at Kaiping, selected stalwart guards of the Yan prince's household to place under Zhong's command, and summoned guards cavalry commanders such as Guan Tong to the capital, so as to weaken Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Regional Commander Song Zhong to move frontier garrisons to camp at Kaiping, drafted the sturdiest guards of the Yan household into Zhong's command, and summoned guards cavalry commanders such as Guan Tong to the capital to weaken Yan.

sentences.zh: 復調北平永清左、右衛官軍分駐彰德、順德，都督徐凱練兵臨清，耿瓛練兵山海關，以控制北平。

translations.literal: He further shifted the left and right garrisons of Yongqing in Beiping to station detachments at Zhangde and Shunde respectively; Regional Commander Xu Kai drilled troops at Linqing and Geng Juan drilled at Shanhaiguan, so as to control Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Troops of the left and right Yongqing garrisons in Beiping were redeployed to Zhangde and Shunde; Regional Commander Xu Kai drilled forces at Linqing and Geng Juan at Shanhaiguan, all to hem in Beiping.

sentences.zh: 皆泰、子澄謀也。

translations.literal: All were schemes of Tai and Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: All of this was the work of Tai and Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 時燕王憂懼，以三子皆在京師，稱病篤，乞三子歸。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Yan was anxious and afraid; with his three sons all in the capital, he claimed grave illness and begged that the three be sent home.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan was then deeply anxious: his three sons were all in the capital, and he claimed grave illness, begging that they be sent home.

sentences.zh: 泰欲遂收之，子澄曰：「不若遣歸，示彼不疑，乃可襲而取也。」

translations.literal: Tai wished to detain them at once; Zicheng said, "Better to send them back, show the other side no suspicion, and then we can strike and seize him."
translations.idiomatic: Tai wanted to detain them at once, but Zicheng said, "Better send them back, show him we suspect nothing, and then we can strike and take him."

sentences.zh: 竟遣還。

translations.literal: In the end they were sent back.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the sons were sent back.

sentences.zh: 未幾，燕師起，王泣誓將吏曰：「陷害諸王，非由天子意，乃奸臣齊泰、黃子澄所為也。」

translations.literal: Before long the Yan army rose; the prince wept and swore to his officers, "The framing of the princes was not the Son of Heaven's intent—it was the work of the traitorous ministers Qi Tai and Huang Zicheng."
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Yan army rose. Weeping, the prince swore to his commanders, "The ruin of the princes was not the Son of Heaven's will—it was wrought by the traitors Qi Tai and Huang Zicheng."

sentences.zh: 始帝信任子澄與泰，聚事削藩。

translations.literal: At first the emperor trusted Zicheng and Tai and gathered affairs toward reducing the feudatories.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor placed his trust in Zicheng and Tai and concentrated policy on reducing the princely domains.

sentences.zh: 兩人本書生，兵事非其所長。

translations.literal: The two were originally literati; military affairs were not their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Both were scholars by origin, and warfare was not their forte.

sentences.zh: 當耿炳文之敗也，子澄謂勝敗常事，不足慮。

translations.literal: When Geng Bingwen was defeated, Zicheng said victory and defeat were ordinary matters and not worth worry.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Bingwen was defeated, Zicheng said that victory and defeat were common in war and not worth fretting over.

sentences.zh: 因薦曹國公李景隆可大任，帝遂以景隆代炳文。

translations.literal: He thereupon recommended Duke of Cao Li Jinglong as fit for great responsibility, and the emperor replaced Bingwen with Jinglong.
translations.idiomatic: He then recommended Duke of Cao Li Jinglong for high command, and the emperor put Jinglong in Bingwen's place.

sentences.zh: 而景隆益無能為，連敗於鄭村壩、白溝河，喪失軍輜士馬數十萬。

translations.literal: Yet Jinglong proved ever more incapable, suffering successive defeats at Zhengcunba and Baigou River and losing several hundred thousand in baggage, troops, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglong proved ever more useless, losing battle after battle at Zhengcunba and on the Baigou River and sacrificing baggage trains, soldiers, and horses by the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 已，又敗於濟南城下。

translations.literal: Later he was defeated again below the walls of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: He was beaten again beneath the walls of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 帝急召景隆還，赦不誅。

translations.literal: The emperor urgently summoned Jinglong back and pardoned him from execution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor urgently recalled Jinglong and spared his life.

sentences.zh: 子澄慟哭，請正其罪。

translations.literal: Zicheng wept in anguish and requested that his crimes be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng wept bitterly and demanded that Jinglong be punished for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 子澄拊膺曰：「大事去矣，薦景隆誤國，萬死不足贖罪！」

translations.literal: Zicheng beat his breast and said, "The great cause is lost! Recommending Jinglong has ruined the state—ten thousand deaths would not atone for the crime!"
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng struck his breast and cried, "The great cause is lost! Recommending Jinglong has betrayed the realm—a thousand deaths would not expiate my guilt!"

sentences.zh: 及燕兵漸南，與齊泰同謫外，密令募兵。

translations.literal: As Yan troops pressed gradually south, he was banished outward together with Qi Tai, with secret orders to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: As Yan forces pushed south, he was exiled together with Qi Tai, with secret orders to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 子澄微服由太湖至蘇州，與知府姚善倡義勤王。

translations.literal: Zicheng went in disguise from Lake Tai to Suzhou and with Prefect Yao Shan raised a loyalist call to rescue the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng traveled in disguise from Lake Tai to Suzhou, where he joined Prefect Yao Shan in rallying loyalists to rescue the throne.

sentences.zh: 善上言：「子澄才足捍難，不宜棄閑遠以快敵人。」

translations.literal: Shan memorialized, "Zicheng's talent is sufficient to meet the crisis; he should not be cast aside in idleness far away to please the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Shan memorialized the throne: "Zicheng's ability is equal to the crisis; he must not be left idle in exile to gratify the enemy."

sentences.zh: 帝復召子澄，未至而京城陷。

translations.literal: The emperor again summoned Zicheng, but before he arrived the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Zicheng again, but before he could arrive the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 欲與善航海乞兵，善不可。

translations.literal: He wished to sail with Shan to beg for troops, but Shan would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted to put to sea with Shan to seek reinforcements, but Shan refused.

sentences.zh: 乃就嘉興楊任謀舉事，為人告，俱被執。

translations.literal: He then went to Yang Ren in Jiaxing to plot action; someone informed on them and both were seized.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned to Yang Ren in Jiaxing to plot an uprising; an informer betrayed them and both were arrested.

sentences.zh: 子澄至，成祖親詰之。

translations.literal: When Zicheng arrived, the Yongle Emperor personally interrogated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zicheng was brought in, the Yongle Emperor questioned him in person.

sentences.zh: 抗辨不屈，磔死。

translations.literal: He argued defiantly and would not yield, and was executed by dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: He answered defiantly and would not submit, and was torn apart by execution.

sentences.zh: 族人無少長皆斬，姻黨悉戍邊。

translations.literal: Clansmen young and old were all beheaded; affines by marriage were all exiled to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Every clansman, young or old, was beheaded, and all connected by marriage were banished to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 一子變姓名為田經，遇赦，家湖廣鹹寧。

translations.literal: One son changed his name to Tian Jing; when an amnesty came he made his home in Xianning in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: One son changed his name to Tian Jing; after an amnesty he settled in Xianning, Huguang.

sentences.zh: 正德中，進士黃表其後雲。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign a jinshi named Huang was his descendant, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengde reign a jinshi named Huang was said to be his descendant.

sentences.zh: 楊任，洪武中由人材起家，歷官袁州知府。

translations.literal: Yang Ren, in the Hongwu reign rose through the talent recruitment route and served as Prefect of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ren entered office in the Hongwu reign through the talent recruitment system and rose to prefect of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時致仕，匿子澄於家，亦磔死。

translations.literal: At that time he had retired; he hid Zicheng in his home and was also executed by dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: He had by then retired from office and was hiding Zicheng in his home; he too was torn apart by execution.

sentences.zh: 二子禮、益俱斬。

translations.literal: His two sons Li and Yi were both beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons, Li and Yi, were both beheaded.

sentences.zh: 親屬戍邊。

translations.literal: Relatives were exiled to frontier garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: His kin were banished to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 方孝孺，字希直，一字希古，寧海人。

translations.literal: Fang Xiaoru, style Xizhi, also styled Xigu, was a native of Ninghai.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xiaoru, styled Xizhi and also known as Xigu, came from Ninghai.

sentences.zh: 父克勤，洪武中循吏，自有傳。

translations.literal: His father Keqin was an exemplary official in the Hongwu reign and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Keqin was a model local official of the Hongwu reign and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 孝孺幼警敏，雙眸炯炯，讀書日盈寸，鄉人目為「小韓子。」

translations.literal: Xiaoru was clever and quick as a child; his two eyes were bright, and his daily reading grew by inches; townspeople called him "Little Han Yu."
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Xiaoru was quick-witted, with a piercing gaze; his reading piled up inch by inch each day, and neighbors called him "Little Han Yu."

sentences.zh: 長從宋濂學，濂門下知名士皆出其下。

translations.literal: Grown, he studied under Song Lian; the famous scholars under Lian's gate all ranked below him.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he studied under Song Lian, and every noted scholar in Lian's school stood beneath him.

sentences.zh: 先輩胡翰、蘇伯衡亦自謂弗如。

translations.literal: Elders Hu Han and Su Boheng also declared themselves his inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Seniors such as Hu Han and Su Boheng admitted they could not match him.

sentences.zh: 孝孺顧末視文藝，恒以明王道、致太平為己任。

translations.literal: Xiaoru looked down on belles-lettres and constantly took clarifying the kingly way and bringing great peace as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoru cared little for literary display and always made it his mission to illuminate the kingly way and bring the realm to peace.

sentences.zh: 嘗臥病，絕糧，家人以告，笑曰：「古人三旬九食，貧豈獨我哉！」

translations.literal: Once he lay ill and was without food; when his family told him, he laughed and said, "The ancients ate only nine meals in thirty days—am I alone in poverty?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, ill in bed and without food, he laughed when his family told him: "The ancients ate only nine meals in thirty days—surely I am not the only poor man!"

sentences.zh: 父克勤坐「空印」事誅，扶喪歸葬，哀動行路。

translations.literal: His father Keqin was executed in the "blank seal" affair; he bore the coffin home for burial, and his grief moved passersby on the road.
translations.idiomatic: His father Keqin was executed in the "blank-seal" affair; Xiaoru bore the coffin home for burial, and his grief moved all who passed on the road.

sentences.zh: 既免喪，復從濂卒業。

translations.literal: After mourning ended, he again followed Lian to complete his studies.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning was over he returned to Lian and finished his training.

sentences.zh: 洪武十五年，以吳沈、揭樞薦，召見。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Hongwu, on recommendation of Wu Shen and Jie Shu, he was summoned for audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Hongwu he was recommended by Wu Shen and Jie Shu and summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 太祖喜其舉止端整，謂皇太子曰：「此莊士，當老其才。」

translations.literal: The founding emperor was pleased with his dignified bearing and told the crown prince, "This is a grave and upright man; his talent should be ripened with age."
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor was pleased with his dignified bearing and told the crown prince, "Here is a man of weight; let his talent mature with years."

sentences.zh: 禮遣還。

translations.literal: He was courteously sent home.
translations.idiomatic: He was courteously sent home.

sentences.zh: 後為仇家所連，逮至京。

translations.literal: Later he was implicated by an enemy family and arrested to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later an enemy family implicated him and he was brought to the capital in custody.

sentences.zh: 太祖見其名，釋之。

translations.literal: The founding emperor saw his name and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his name, the founding emperor ordered his release.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，又以薦召至。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was again summoned on recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was summoned again on recommendation.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「今非用孝孺時。」

translations.literal: The founding emperor said, "Now is not the time to employ Xiaoru."
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor said, "This is not yet the time to use Xiaoru."

sentences.zh: 除漢中教授，日與諸生講學不倦。

translations.literal: He was appointed professor at Hanzhong and daily lectured students without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed professor at Hanzhong, where he lectured his students day after day without tiring.

sentences.zh: 蜀獻王聞其賢，聘為世子師。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Shu, hearing of his worth, engaged him as tutor to the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Shu, hearing of his reputation, engaged him as tutor to the heir.

sentences.zh: 每見，陳說道德。

translations.literal: At each meeting he expounded moral principle.
translations.idiomatic: At every audience he expounded moral principle.

sentences.zh: 王尊以殊禮，名其讀書之廬曰「正學。」

translations.literal: The prince honored him with special ceremony and named his study hall "Correct Learning."
translations.idiomatic: The prince honored him with exceptional ceremony and named his study "Correct Learning."

sentences.zh: 及惠帝即位，召為翰林侍講。明年遷侍講學士，國家大政事輒咨之。帝好讀書，每有疑，即召使講解。臨朝奏事，臣僚面議可否，或命孝孺就扆前批答。時修《太祖實錄》及《類要》諸書，孝孺皆為總裁。更定官制，孝孺改文學博士。燕兵起，廷議討之，詔檄皆出其手。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui came to the throne, he summoned Xiaoru to be Hanlin Attendant Lecturer. The next year he was promoted to Attendant Lecturer Academician, and whenever there were major affairs of state he was consulted. The emperor liked reading books; whenever he had doubts, he summoned Xiaoru to explain them. When matters were presented at court and ministers discussed their approval or rejection face to face, the emperor sometimes ordered Xiaoru to come before the screen and draft the reply. At the time the Veritable Records of Taizu, the Classified Essentials, and other books were being compiled, and Xiaoru served as chief editor for all of them. When the official system was revised, Xiaoru was changed to Doctor of Literature. When Yan troops rose, the court debated campaigning against them, and the edicts and proclamations all came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui came to the throne, he summoned Xiaoru as Hanlin Attendant Lecturer. The following year Xiaoru was promoted to Attendant Lecturer Academician, and he was consulted on every major affair of state. The emperor loved reading; whenever he had a question, he summoned Xiaoru to explain it. When business was presented at court and ministers debated approval or rejection in person, the emperor sometimes had Xiaoru come before the screen and draft the reply. Xiaoru served as chief editor for the Veritable Records of Taizu, the Classified Essentials, and the other works then being compiled. When the bureaucracy was revised, he became Doctor of Literature. After Yan troops rose, the court debated their suppression, and the edicts and proclamations all came from his hand.

sentences.zh: 建文三年，燕兵掠大名。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianwen, Yan troops raided Daming.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Jianwen reign Yan forces raided Daming.

sentences.zh: 王聞齊、黃已竄，上書請罷盛庸、吳傑、平安兵。

translations.literal: The prince, hearing that Qi and Huang had fled, submitted a memorial requesting that the armies of Sheng Yong, Wu Jie, and Ping An be disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: The prince, hearing that Qi and Huang had fled, memorialized asking that the armies of Sheng Yong, Wu Jie, and Ping An be stood down.

sentences.zh: 孝孺建議曰：「燕兵久頓大名，天暑雨，當不戰自疲。

translations.literal: Xiaoru advised, "The Yan army has long been stalled at Daming; heaven is hot and rainy—they should weary without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoru advised, "The Yan army has lingered long at Daming; in this heat and rain it should wear itself out without a battle.

sentences.zh: 急令遼東諸將入山海關攻永平；

translations.literal: Urgently order the generals of Liaodong to enter Shanhaiguan and attack Yongping;
translations.idiomatic: Order the Liaodong generals at once through Shanhaiguan to strike Yongping;

sentences.zh: 真定諸將渡盧溝搗北平，彼必歸救。

translations.literal: the generals of Zhending should cross the Lugou to strike at Beiping—the enemy is sure to return to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: and the Zhending commanders should cross the Lugou to threaten Beiping, forcing the enemy to turn back.

sentences.zh: 我以大兵躡其後，可成擒也。

translations.literal: We follow with a great army and can take them captive.
translations.idiomatic: Our main force can then fall on their rear and take them captive.

sentences.zh: 今其奏事適至，宜且與報書，往返逾月，使其將士心懈。

translations.literal: Now his memorial has just arrived; we should for the moment send a reply, and with exchanges over more than a month their officers and soldiers will grow slack in heart.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial has just arrived; we should answer it and let a month of back-and-forth correspondence sap their officers' and soldiers' resolve.

sentences.zh: 我謀定勢合，進而蹴之，不難矣。」

translations.literal: When our plan is settled and forces aligned, advancing to trample them will not be hard."
translations.idiomatic: Once our plans are set and our forces in place, we can press forward and crush them with ease."

sentences.zh: 帝以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought it right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 命孝孺草詔，遣大理寺少卿薛嵓馳報燕，盡赦燕罪，使罷兵歸藩。

translations.literal: He ordered Xiaoru to draft an edict and sent Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Xue Yan posthaste to report to Yan, fully pardoning Yan's crimes and ordering cessation of troops and return to the fief.
translations.idiomatic: He had Xiaoru draft an edict and sent Vice Minister Xue Yan of the Court of Judicial Review posthaste to Yan with a full pardon and orders to stand down and return to his fief.

sentences.zh: 又為宣諭數千言授嵓，持至燕軍中，密散諸將士。

translations.literal: He also composed a proclamation of several thousand words for Yan to carry, to be taken to the Yan army and secretly distributed among the generals and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoru also composed a proclamation of several thousand words for Yan to carry into the Yan camp and distribute secretly among the officers and men.

sentences.zh: 比至，嵓匿宣諭不敢出，燕王亦不奉詔。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Yan hid the proclamation and dared not produce it; the Prince of Yan also did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan arrived he hid the proclamation and dared not release it; the Prince of Yan likewise ignored the edict.

sentences.zh: 五月，吳傑、平安、盛庸發兵擾燕餉道。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Wu Jie, Ping An, and Sheng Yong launched troops to harass Yan's supply routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Wu Jie, Ping An, and Sheng Yong moved troops to cut Yan's supply lines.

sentences.zh: 燕王復遣指揮武勝上書，伸前請。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan again sent Commander Wu Sheng to submit a memorial renewing his earlier request.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan again sent Commander Wu Sheng with a memorial renewing his earlier plea.

sentences.zh: 帝將許之。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was on the point of granting it.

sentences.zh: 孝孺曰：「兵罷，不可復聚，願毋為所惑。」

translations.literal: Xiaoru said, "Once troops are disbanded they cannot be gathered again—may Your Majesty not be deceived."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoru said, "Once an army is stood down it cannot be reassembled—do not let him deceive you."

sentences.zh: 帝乃誅勝以絕燕。

translations.literal: The emperor then executed Sheng to cut off Yan's hope.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then executed Sheng to shut off any further overtures from Yan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，燕兵掠沛縣，燒糧艘。

translations.literal: Before long Yan troops raided Pei County and burned grain transports.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yan forces raided Pei County and burned the grain fleet.

sentences.zh: 時河北師老無功，而德州又饋餉道絕，孝孺深以為憂。

translations.literal: At that time the Hebei army was weary without success, and at Dezhou the supply route was cut; Xiaoru was deeply troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The Hebei armies were exhausted and achieving nothing, and the supply route to Dezhou was severed; Xiaoru was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 以燕世子仁厚，其弟高煦狡譎，有寵於燕王，嘗欲奪嫡，謀以計間之，使內亂。

translations.literal: Because the Yan heir was benevolent and his younger brother Gaoxu was crafty and cunning, favored by the Prince of Yan and once wishing to seize the succession, he plotted to set them at odds by stratagem and cause internal disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the Yan heir to be mild and his younger brother Gaoxu crafty and favored by the prince—and that Gaoxu had once sought to displace his brother—he plotted to drive a wedge between them and sow internal strife.

sentences.zh: 乃建議白帝：遣錦衣衛千戶張安賫璽書往北平，賜世子。

translations.literal: He therefore advised the emperor: send Embroidered Uniform Guard battalion commander Zhang An bearing the imperial seal letter to Beiping to bestow it on the heir.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore proposed that the emperor send Zhang An of the Embroidered Uniform Guard with an imperial letter under seal to Beiping, to be conferred on the heir alone.

sentences.zh: 世子得書不啟封，並安送燕軍前。

translations.literal: The heir received the letter without opening it and sent An together with it to the Yan army's front.
translations.idiomatic: The heir received the letter unopened and sent it on with An to his father's camp.

sentences.zh: 間不得行。

translations.literal: The estrangement could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The stratagem failed.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，燕兵至江北，帝下詔征四方兵。

translations.literal: The next year in the fifth month, when Yan troops reached the north bank of the Yangzi, the emperor issued an edict calling up troops from all quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The following fifth month, as Yan forces reached the north bank of the Yangzi, the emperor issued an edict mobilizing troops from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 孝孺曰：「事急矣。

translations.literal: Xiaoru said, "The matter is urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoru said, "Matters are desperate.

sentences.zh: 遣人許以割地，稽延數日，東南募兵漸集。

translations.literal: Send someone promising to cede territory and delay several days; troops raised in the southeast will gradually gather.
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys offering to cede territory and gain a few days' delay; troops raised in the southeast will gradually assemble.

sentences.zh: 北軍不長舟楫，決戰江上，勝負未可知也。」

translations.literal: Northern troops are not skilled on water; if we fight decisively on the river, victory and defeat are not yet knowable."
translations.idiomatic: Northern armies are weak on the water; a decisive battle on the river might still go either way."

sentences.zh: 帝遣慶成郡主往燕軍，陳其說。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the Princess of Qingcheng to the Yan army to set forth this plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the Princess of Qingcheng to the Yan camp to present the offer.

sentences.zh: 燕王不聽。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan refused.

sentences.zh: 帝命諸將集舟師江上。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the generals to assemble a fleet on the river.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered his generals to assemble a fleet on the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 而陳瑄以戰艦降燕，燕兵遂渡江。

translations.literal: But Chen Xuan surrendered his warships to Yan, and Yan troops thereupon crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: But Chen Xuan surrendered his warships to Yan, and the Yan army crossed the river.

sentences.zh: 時六月乙卯也。

translations.literal: It was the yimao day of the sixth month.
translations.idiomatic: This was on the yimao day of the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 帝憂懼，或勸帝他幸，圖興復。

translations.literal: The emperor was anxious and afraid; some urged him to go elsewhere and plot restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was stricken with fear; some urged him to flee the capital and plot restoration elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 孝孺力請守京城以待援兵，即事不濟，當死社稷。

translations.literal: Xiaoru urgently pleaded to hold the capital and await relief troops; even if the affair did not succeed, one should die for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoru urgently pleaded to hold the capital and await relief; even if all failed, they should die with the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，金川門啟，燕兵入，帝自焚。

translations.literal: On yichou, the Jinchuan Gate was opened, Yan troops entered, and the emperor burned himself.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou the Jinchuan Gate was opened; Yan troops entered, and the emperor burned himself to death.

sentences.zh: 是日，孝孺被執下獄。

translations.literal: That day Xiaoru was seized and cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Xiaoru was arrested and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 先是，成祖發北平，姚廣孝以孝孺為托，曰：「城下之日，彼必不降，幸勿殺之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Yongle Emperor set out from Beiping, Yao Guangxiao had entrusted him concerning Xiaoru, saying, "On the day the city is taken, he surely will not submit—pray do not kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Yongle Emperor marched from Beiping, Yao Guangxiao had begged him concerning Xiaoru: "When the city falls he will surely not submit—please do not kill him.

sentences.zh: 殺孝孺，天下讀書種子絕矣。」

translations.literal: Kill Xiaoru, and the seed of learning throughout the realm is cut off."
translations.idiomatic: Kill Xiaoru, and the seed of learning in the empire is extinguished."

sentences.zh: 成祖頷之。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor nodded in assent.

sentences.zh: 至是欲使草詔。

translations.literal: Now he wished to have him draft the accession proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: Now he wished to have Xiaoru draft the accession edict.

sentences.zh: 召至，悲慟聲徹殿陛。

translations.literal: Summoned before the throne, his grief and anguish filled the hall.
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned, his grief and sobbing filled the hall.

sentences.zh: 成祖降榻，勞曰：「先生毋自苦，予欲法周公輔成王耳。」

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor descended from the couch and comforted him, saying, "Sir, do not torment yourself—I mean only to follow the Duke of Zhou in assisting King Cheng."
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor stepped down from the throne and comforted him: "Sir, do not torment yourself—I mean only to follow the Duke of Zhou in assisting King Cheng."

sentences.zh: 孝孺曰：「成王安在？」

translations.literal: Xiaoru said, "Where is King Cheng?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoru asked, "Where is King Cheng?"

sentences.zh: 成祖曰：「彼自焚死。」

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor said, "He burned himself to death."
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor said, "He burned himself to death."

sentences.zh: 孝孺曰：「何不立成王之子？」

translations.literal: Xiaoru said, "Why not establish King Cheng's son?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoru asked, "Why not enthrone King Cheng's son?"

sentences.zh: 成祖曰：「國賴長君。」

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor said, "The state relies on an elder ruler."
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor said, "The realm needs a mature ruler."

sentences.zh: 孝孺曰：「何不立成王之弟？」

translations.literal: Xiaoru said, "Why not establish King Cheng's younger brother?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoru asked, "Why not enthrone King Cheng's younger brother?"

sentences.zh: 成祖曰：「此朕家事。」

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor said, "This is a family matter of mine."
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor said, "That is my family's affair."

sentences.zh: 顧左右授筆劄，曰：「詔天下，非先生草不可」孝孺投筆於地，且哭且罵曰：「死即死耳，詔不可草。」

translations.literal: He looked to attendants and handed brush and paper, saying, "To proclaim to the realm—no one but you, sir, can draft it." Xiaoru threw the brush to the ground and, weeping and cursing, said, "Death is death—no edict will I draft."
translations.idiomatic: He turned to his attendants for brush and paper and said, "To proclaim the realm—no one but you, sir, can draft it." Xiaoru flung the brush to the floor and, weeping and cursing, cried, "Death is death—I will not draft your edict."

sentences.zh: 成祖怒，命磔諸市。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor was enraged and ordered him torn apart in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor flew into a rage and ordered him torn apart in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 孝孺慨然就死，作絕命詞曰：「天降亂離兮孰知其由，奸臣得計兮謀國用猶。

translations.literal: Xiaoru went to his death with high resolve and composed a final verse: "Heaven sends chaos and separation—who knows its cause? Traitors gain their schemes and still plot the state.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoru went to his death with high resolve and composed a final verse: "Heaven sends chaos and separation—who knows its cause? Traitors win their schemes and still govern the realm.

sentences.zh: 忠臣發憤兮血淚交流，以此殉君兮抑又何求？

translations.literal: Loyal ministers burst with rage, blood and tears streaming; to die thus for our lord—what more could we seek?
translations.idiomatic: Loyal ministers burn with rage, blood and tears streaming down; to die thus for our lord—what more could we ask?

sentences.zh: 鳴呼哀哉兮庶不我尤！」

translations.literal: Alas! How tragic! May none blame me!"
translations.idiomatic: Alas! How tragic! May none hold this against me!"

sentences.zh: 時年四十有六。

translations.literal: He was then forty-six years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-six years old.

sentences.zh: 其門人德慶侯廖永忠之孫鏞與其弟銘，檢遺骸瘞聚寶門外山上。

translations.literal: His disciples, Marquis of Deqing Liao Yongzhong's grandsons Yong and his younger brother Ming, gathered his remains and buried them on the hill outside the Jubao Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples, the grandsons Yong and Ming of Marquis Liao Yongzhong of Deqing, gathered his remains and buried them on the hill outside the Jubao Gate.

sentences.zh: 孝孺有兄孝聞，力學篤行，先孝孺死。

translations.literal: Xiaoru had an elder brother Xiaowen, who studied strenuously and practiced virtue steadfastly and died before Xiaoru.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoru had an elder brother, Xiaowen, who studied hard and lived uprightly and died before him.

sentences.zh: 弟孝友與孝孺同就戮，亦賦詩一章而死。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xiaoyou was executed together with Xiaoru and also composed a poem before dying.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiaoyou was executed with him and likewise composed a poem before he died.

sentences.zh: 妻鄭及二子中憲、中愈先自經死，二女投秦淮河死。

translations.literal: His wife Zheng and his two sons Zhongxian and Zhongyu hanged themselves first; his two daughters threw themselves into the Qinhuai River and died.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Zheng and his sons Zhongxian and Zhongyu hanged themselves first; his two daughters drowned themselves in the Qinhuai River.

sentences.zh: 孝孺工文章，醇深雄邁。

translations.literal: Xiaoru was skilled in literary composition, pure, deep, bold, and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoru was a master of prose—grave, deep, and boldly expansive in manner.

sentences.zh: 每一篇出，海內爭相傳誦。

translations.literal: Whenever a piece appeared, the realm vied to copy and recite it.
translations.idiomatic: Each new essay set the empire copying and reciting it in rivalry.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，藏孝孺文者罪至死。

translations.literal: In the Yongle reign, those who hid Xiaoru's writings were punished up to death.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongle, hiding Xiaoru's writings was a capital offense.

sentences.zh: 門人王稌潛錄為《侯城集》，故後得行於世。

translations.literal: His disciple Wang Zhi secretly recorded them as the Houcheng Collection, and so later they could circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His disciple Wang Zhi secretly compiled them as the Houcheng Collection, which is how they later reached the world.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，諭禮部：「建文諸臣，已蒙顯戮。家屬籍在官者，悉宥為民，還其田土。其外親戍邊者，留一人戍所，余放還。」萬歷十三年三月，釋坐孝孺謫戍者後裔，浙江、江西、福建、四川、廣東凡千三百餘人。而孝孺絕無後，惟克勤弟克家有子曰孝復。洪武二十五年嘗上書闕下，請減信國公湯和所加寧海賦，謫戍慶遠衛，以軍籍獲免。孝復子琬，後亦得釋為民。世宗時，松江人俞斌自稱孝孺後，一時士大夫信之，為纂《歸宗錄》。既而方氏察其偽，言於官，乃已。神宗初，有詔褒錄建文忠臣，建表忠祠於南京，首徐輝祖，次孝孺雲。

translations.literal: When Renzong came to the throne, he instructed the Ministry of Rites: "The Jianwen ministers have already suffered manifest execution. Those of their families registered with the government are all to be pardoned as commoners, and their fields and lands returned. As for outside relatives garrisoned on the frontier, leave one person at the garrison place and release the rest to return." In the third month of Wanli year thirteen, the descendants of those exiled to garrisons on account of Xiaoru were released, more than thirteen hundred persons in all from Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, Sichuan, and Guangdong. Xiaoru himself had no descendants at all. Only Keqin's younger brother Kejia had a son named Xiaofu. In Hongwu year twenty-five Xiaofu had once submitted a letter at the palace gate requesting that the Ninghai taxes added by Tang He, Duke of Xinguo, be reduced; he was exiled to Qingyuan Guard, and because he was on the military rolls he escaped. Xiaofu's son Wan was later also released as a commoner. In Shizong's time, Yu Bin of Songjiang claimed to be a descendant of Xiaoru, and for a time scholar-officials believed him and compiled for him the Guizong lu. Later the Fang clan detected the fraud and reported it to the authorities, and the matter ended. At the beginning of Shenzong's reign, an edict commended and recorded the loyal ministers of Jianwen and built the Shrine for Manifesting Loyalty at Nanjing; Xu Huizu was first, and Xiaoru second, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong came to the throne, he instructed the Ministry of Rites: "The Jianwen ministers have already suffered public execution. All family members registered with the authorities are to be pardoned as commoners, and their fields and lands returned. Of their outside relatives exiled to frontier garrisons, leave one person at the garrison and release the rest to go home." In the third month of Wanli 13, descendants of those exiled to garrisons because of Xiaoru were released, over thirteen hundred people from Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, Sichuan, and Guangdong. Xiaoru himself left no descendants. Only Keqin's younger brother Kejia had a son named Xiaofu. In Hongwu 25 Xiaofu had submitted a letter at the palace gate asking that the added Ninghai taxes imposed by Tang He, Duke of Xinguo, be reduced; he was exiled to Qingyuan Guard, and his military registration spared him. Xiaofu's son Wan was later also released as a commoner. Under Shizong, Yu Bin of Songjiang claimed to be Xiaoru's descendant, and for a time scholar-officials believed him and compiled the Guizong lu for him. Later the Fang clan discovered the fraud and reported it to the authorities, ending the matter. Early under Shenzong, an edict honored and recorded the loyal ministers of Jianwen and established the Shrine for Manifesting Loyalty in Nanjing, with Xu Huizu first and Xiaoru second.

sentences.zh: 孝孺之死，宗族親友前後坐誅者數百人。

translations.literal: At Xiaoru's death, clansmen and friends implicated before and after numbered several hundred put to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the wake of Xiaoru's death, several hundred kinsmen and associates were executed by implication.

sentences.zh: 其門下士有以身殉者，盧原質、鄭公智、林嘉猷，皆寧海人。

translations.literal: Among his disciples were those who gave their lives in martyrdom: Lu Yuanzhi, Zheng Gongzhi, and Lin Jiayou—all natives of Ninghai.
translations.idiomatic: Among his disciples who died with him were Lu Yuanzhi, Zheng Gongzhi, and Lin Jiayou, all from Ninghai.

sentences.zh: 原質字希魯，孝孺姑子也。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi, style Xilu, was Xiaoru's nephew by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi, styled Xilu, was Xiaoru's nephew by marriage.

sentences.zh: 由進士授編修，歷官太常少卿。

translations.literal: Through the jinshi degree he was appointed Compiler and rose to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi, he became a compiler and rose to Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 建文時，屢有建白。

translations.literal: In the Jianwen reign he repeatedly offered proposals.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwen reign he offered counsel again and again.

sentences.zh: 燕兵至，不屈，與弟原樸等皆被殺。

translations.literal: When Yan troops arrived he would not yield; together with his younger brother Yuanpu and others he was all killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan forces arrived he refused to submit and was killed together with his younger brother Yuanpu and others.

sentences.zh: 公智字叔貞；

translations.literal: Gongzhi, style Shuzhen;
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhi, styled Shuzhen;

sentences.zh: 嘉猷名升，以字行。

translations.literal: Jiayou's given name was Sheng; he was known by his style.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayou's given name was Sheng, but he was known by his style.

sentences.zh: 皆師事孝孺。

translations.literal: Both took Xiaoru as their teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Both studied under Xiaoru.

sentences.zh: 孝孺嘗曰：「匡我者，二子也。」

translations.literal: Xiaoru once said, "Those who set me right are these two men."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoru once said, "These two are the men who set me straight."

sentences.zh: 公智以賢良舉，為御史有聲。

translations.literal: Gongzhi was raised through the worthy-and-good selection and as censor won renown.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhi entered office through the worthy-and-good selection and won renown as a censor.

sentences.zh: 嘉猷，洪武丙子以儒士校文四川。

translations.literal: Jiayou, in bingzi of Hongwu, as a Confucian scholar graded examination papers in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingzi year of Hongwu, Jiayou graded examination papers in Sichuan as a Confucian scholar.

sentences.zh: 建文初，入史館為編修。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen he entered the Historiography Institute as Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianwen he entered the Historiography Institute as compiler.

sentences.zh: 尋遷陜西僉事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Commissioner in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice commissioner in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 嘗以事入燕邸，知高煦謀傾世子狀。

translations.literal: Once on business he entered the Yan residence and learned how Gaoxu plotted to overturn the heir.
translations.idiomatic: On one mission he entered the Yan residence and learned of Gaoxu's plot against the heir.

sentences.zh: 孝孺間燕之謀，實嘉猷發之。

translations.literal: Xiaoru's estrangement stratagem against Yan was in fact initiated by Jiayou.
translations.idiomatic: It was Jiayou who first alerted Xiaoru to Yan's designs.

sentences.zh: 胡子昭，字仲常，初名誌高。

translations.literal: Hu Zizhao, style Zhongchang, originally named Zhigao.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zizhao, styled Zhongchang, was originally named Zhigao.

sentences.zh: 榮縣人。

translations.literal: A native of Rong County.
translations.idiomatic: He came from Rong County.

sentences.zh: 孝孺為漢中教授時往從學，蜀獻王薦為縣訓導。

translations.literal: When Xiaoru was professor at Hanzhong he went to study under him; Prince Xian of Shu recommended him as county instructor.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaoru taught at Hanzhong, Zizhao went to study with him; Prince Xian of Shu recommended him as county instructor.

sentences.zh: 建文初，與修《太祖實錄》，授檢討。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen he took part in compiling the Veritable Records of the Founding Emperor and was appointed Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianwen he helped compile the Veritable Records of the Founding Emperor and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 累遷至刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He rose in successive transfers to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 鄭居貞，閩人。

translations.literal: Zheng Juzhen was a native of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Juzhen came from Fujian.

sentences.zh: 與孝孺友善，以明經歷官鞏昌通判、河南參政。

translations.literal: He was friendly with Xiaoru; through the classics examination he served as Tongpan of Gongchang and Administrative Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: A friend of Xiaoru, he entered office through the classics examination and served as subprefect of Gongchang and administrative commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 所至有善績。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he left good record.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he left a record of good governance.

sentences.zh: 孝孺教授漢中，居貞作《鳳雛行》勖之。

translations.literal: When Xiaoru taught at Hanzhong, Juzhen composed "Song of the Phoenix Chick" to encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaoru taught at Hanzhong, Juzhen wrote "Song of the Phoenix Chick" to encourage him.

sentences.zh: 諸人皆坐黨誅死。

translations.literal: All these men were put to death for party association.
translations.idiomatic: All were executed as associates of Xiaoru's faction.

sentences.zh: 孝孺主應天鄉試，所得士有長洲劉政、桐城方法。

translations.literal: When Xiaoru presided over the metropolitan provincial examination for Yingtian, among the men he obtained were Liu Zheng of Changzhou and Fang Fa of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaoru presided over the Yingtian provincial examination, among those he passed were Liu Zheng of Changzhou and Fang Fa of Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 政，字仲理。

translations.literal: Zheng, style Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, styled Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 燕兵起，草《平燕策》，將上之，以病為家人所沮。

translations.literal: When Yan troops rose he drafted "Plan to Pacify Yan" and was about to submit it, but illness and his family's discouragement stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army rose he drafted a "Plan to Pacify Yan" and was about to submit it, but illness and his family's opposition held him back.

sentences.zh: 及聞孝孺死，遂嘔血卒。

translations.literal: When he heard of Xiaoru's death he vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing of Xiaoru's death he vomited blood and died.

sentences.zh: 法，字伯通。

translations.literal: Fa, style Botong.
translations.idiomatic: Fa, styled Botong.

sentences.zh: 官四川都司斷事。

translations.literal: He served as judicial officer of the Sichuan Regional Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judicial officer of the Sichuan regional military commission.

sentences.zh: 諸司表賀成祖登極，當署名，不肯，投筆出。

translations.literal: When the various offices submitted congratulatory memorials on the Yongle Emperor's accession, he was to sign but refused, threw down the brush, and left.
translations.idiomatic: When the offices submitted congratulations on the Yongle Emperor's accession, he was required to sign but refused, flung down his brush, and walked out.

sentences.zh: 被逮，次望江，瞻拜鄉里曰：「得望我先人廬舍足矣。」

translations.literal: Seized, he halted at Wangjiang and gazed toward his home district, saying, "To glimpse my forebears' dwelling is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Arrested, he paused at Wangjiang and gazed toward home, saying, "To see my ancestors' dwelling once more is enough."

sentences.zh: 自沈於江。

translations.literal: He drowned himself in the river.
translations.idiomatic: He drowned himself in the river.

sentences.zh: 成祖既殺孝孺，以草詔屬侍讀樓璉。

translations.literal: After the Yongle Emperor had killed Xiaoru, he assigned drafting the accession edict to Reader-in-Waiting Lou Lian.
translations.idiomatic: After killing Xiaoru, the Yongle Emperor charged Reader-in-Waiting Lou Lian with drafting the accession edict.

sentences.zh: 璉，金華人，嘗從宋濂學。

translations.literal: Lian, a native of Jinhua, had once studied under Song Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Lian, from Jinhua, had studied under Song Lian.

sentences.zh: 承命不敢辭。

translations.literal: Receiving the order he dared not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted the order and dared not refuse.

sentences.zh: 歸語妻子曰：「我固甘死，正恐累汝輩耳。」

translations.literal: Returning home he told his wife and children, "I am willing to die, but I fear only that I will bring harm upon you all."
translations.idiomatic: At home he told his wife and children, "I am ready to die, but I fear only that I will bring ruin on you."

sentences.zh: 其夕，遂自經。

translations.literal: That evening he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: That night he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 或曰草詔乃括蒼王景，或曰無錫王達雲。

translations.literal: Some say the edict was drafted by Wang Jing of Kuocang; others say Wang Dayun of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Some say the edict was drafted by Wang Jing of Kuocang; others say by Wang Dayun of Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 練子寧，名安，以字行，新淦人。

translations.literal: Lian Zining, given name An, known by his style, was a native of Xingan.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Zining, whose given name was An but who was known by his style, came from Xingan.

sentences.zh: 父伯尚，工詩。

translations.literal: His father Boshang was skilled in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Boshang was a skilled poet.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，官起居註。

translations.literal: In early Hongwu he served as Recorder of Imperial Actions.
translations.idiomatic: In early Hongwu he served as recorder of imperial actions.

sentences.zh: 以直言謫外任，終鎮安通判。

translations.literal: For outspoken words he was demoted to outer appointment and ended as Tongpan of Zhen'an.
translations.idiomatic: For blunt speech he was demoted to provincial service and ended his career as subprefect of Zhen'an.

sentences.zh: 子寧英邁不群，十八年，以貢士廷試對策，力言：「天之生材有限，陛下忍以區區小故，縱無窮之誅，何以為治？」

translations.literal: Zining was outstanding and peerless; in the eighteenth year, as a tribute scholar in the palace examination he answered forcefully: "Heaven's production of talent is limited—can Your Majesty bear, for trifling causes, to unleash endless executions? How is this governance?"
translations.idiomatic: Zining was brilliant and stood apart from the crowd. In the eighteenth year, answering at the palace examination as a tribute scholar, he declared forcefully: "Heaven produces talent in limited measure—how can Your Majesty, for petty causes, unleash endless executions and still govern well?"

sentences.zh: 太祖善其意，擢一甲第二，授翰林修撰。

translations.literal: The founding emperor approved his intent and promoted him second in the first rank, appointing him Hanlin Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor approved his point and ranked him second in the first class, appointing him Hanlin reviser.

sentences.zh: 丁母艱，力行古禮。

translations.literal: In mourning for his mother he strenuously practiced ancient rites.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning his mother, he practiced the ancient rites with strict devotion.

sentences.zh: 服闋，復官，歷遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he resumed office and rose in transfer to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he returned to office and rose to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 建文初，與方孝孺並見信用，改吏部左侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen he and Fang Xiaoru were alike trusted and employed; he was changed to Left Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianwen he and Fang Xiaoru were equally trusted; he was made Left Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 以賢否進退為己任，多所建白。

translations.literal: He took advancing the worthy and retiring the unworthy as his own charge and offered many proposals.
translations.idiomatic: He made it his duty to advance the worthy and remove the unworthy, and offered much counsel.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 燕師起，李景隆北征屢敗，召還。

translations.literal: When the Yan army rose, Li Jinglong's northern campaign suffered repeated defeats and he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army rose, Li Jinglong's northern campaign met repeated defeat and he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 子寧從朝中執數其罪，請誅之。

translations.literal: Zining seized him in court and enumerated his crimes, requesting execution.
translations.idiomatic: Zining seized him in open court, recited his crimes, and demanded his execution.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 憤激叩首大呼曰：「壞陛下事者，此賊也。

translations.literal: In furious agitation he knocked his head and cried aloud, "The man who has ruined Your Majesty's affairs is this traitor.
translations.idiomatic: In a fury he struck his head on the floor in a kowtow and cried, "This traitor is the man who has ruined Your Majesty's cause!

sentences.zh: 臣備員執法，不能為朝廷除賣國奸，死有余罪。

translations.literal: Your servant holds a nominal post in law enforcement yet cannot rid the court of a traitor who sells the state—death would still leave guilt.
translations.idiomatic: I hold a nominal post as chief of law enforcement yet cannot rid the court of a traitor who sells the realm—even death would not expiate my guilt.

sentences.zh: 即陛下赦景隆，必無赦臣！」

translations.literal: Even if Your Majesty pardons Jinglong, you surely will not pardon your servant!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if Your Majesty pardons Jinglong, you will surely not pardon me!"

sentences.zh: 因大哭求死，帝為罷朝。

translations.literal: He thereupon wept greatly and begged for death; the emperor dismissed court on his account.
translations.idiomatic: He burst into tears and begged for death, and the emperor dismissed court.

sentences.zh: 宗人府經歷宋徵、御史葉希賢皆抗疏言景隆失律喪師，懷二心，宜誅。

translations.literal: Imperial Clan Court Registrar Song Zheng and Censor Ye Xixian both submitted defiant memorials saying Jinglong had violated discipline, lost armies, harbored divided loyalty, and ought to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Clan Court registrar Song Zheng and Censor Ye Xixian both submitted bold memorials accusing Jinglong of violating discipline, losing armies, harboring divided loyalty, and deserving execution.

sentences.zh: 並不納。

translations.literal: None was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: None of this was heeded.

sentences.zh: 燕師既渡淮，靖江府長史蕭用道、衡府紀善周是修上書論大計，指斥用事者。

translations.literal: After Yan troops had crossed the Huai, Princely Establishment Chief Clerk Xiao Yongdao of Jingjiang and Princely Establishment Recorder Zhou Shixiu of Heng submitted memorials on the grand strategy, denouncing those in power.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan forces crossed the Huai, Xiao Yongdao, chief clerk of the Jingjiang princely establishment, and Zhou Shixiu, recorder of the Heng establishment, memorialized on grand strategy and denounced those in power.

sentences.zh: 書下廷臣議，用事者盛氣以詬二人。

translations.literal: The memorials were sent down for court discussion; those in power vented their wrath in reviling the two men.
translations.idiomatic: The memorials were referred to the court for discussion, and those in power assailed the two men with furious abuse.

sentences.zh: 子寧曰：「國事至此，尚不能容言者耶？」

translations.literal: Zining said, "The state's affairs have come to this—can we still not tolerate those who speak?"
translations.idiomatic: Zining said, "Matters have come to this pass—can we still not tolerate men who speak out?"

sentences.zh: 詬者愧而止。

translations.literal: The revilers, ashamed, ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The abusers fell silent in shame.

sentences.zh: 燕王即位，縛子寧至。語不遜，磔死。族其家，姻戚俱戍邊。子寧從子大亨，官嘉定知縣。聞變，同妻沈劉家河死。裏人徐子權以進士為刑部主事，聞子寧死，慟哭賦詩自經。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan came to the throne, he had Zining bound and brought in. Zining's words were defiant, and he was dismembered. His family was exterminated, and his relatives by marriage were all sent to garrison the frontier. Zining's nephew Daheng served as magistrate of Jiading. Hearing of the change, he died together with his wife Shen at Liu Family River. A fellow villager, Xu Ziquan, who had passed the jinshi examination and served as a supervising secretary in the Ministry of Justice, heard that Zining had died, wept bitterly, composed a poem, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan took the throne, Zining was bound and brought before him. He spoke defiantly and was dismembered. His household was exterminated, and his in-laws were all sent to frontier garrisons. Zining's nephew Daheng, magistrate of Jiading, heard of the upheaval and died with his wife Shen at Liu Family River. A fellow villager, Xu Ziquan, a jinshi serving as a supervising secretary in the Ministry of Justice, heard of Zining's death, wept bitterly, composed a poem, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 子寧善文章，孝孺稱其多學而文。

translations.literal: Zining was skilled in literary composition; Xiaoru praised him as broadly learned and accomplished in letters.
translations.idiomatic: Zining was a fine writer; Xiaoru praised him as learned and accomplished in letters.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，王佐刻其遺文曰《金川玉屑集》。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi reign Wang Zuo printed his surviving writings as the Jinchuan Jade Fragments Collection.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongzhi reign Wang Zuo printed his surviving writings as the Jinchuan Jade Fragments Collection.

sentences.zh: 提學副使李夢陽立金川書院祀子寧，名其堂曰「浩然」。

translations.literal: Education Intendant Vice Commissioner Li Mengyang established Jinchuan Academy to sacrifice to Zining and named its hall "Vast Integrity."
translations.idiomatic: Education intendant Li Mengyang founded Jinchuan Academy to honor Zining and named its hall "Vast Integrity."

sentences.zh: 徵，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Zheng—his origin is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's place of origin is unknown.

sentences.zh: 嘗疏請削罪藩屬籍。

translations.literal: He once memorialized requesting that guilty princes be struck from the clan register.
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized asking that guilty princes be removed from the imperial clan rolls.

sentences.zh: 燕師入，不屈，並妻子俱死。

translations.literal: When Yan troops entered he would not yield; wife and children all died together.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan forces entered the capital he refused to submit; he and his wife and children all died.

sentences.zh: 希賢，松陽人。

translations.literal: Xixian was a native of Songyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian came from Songyang.

sentences.zh: 亦坐奸黨被殺。

translations.literal: He too was killed for association with the traitor faction.
translations.idiomatic: He too was killed as a member of the traitor faction.

sentences.zh: 或曰去為僧，號雪庵和尚雲。

translations.literal: Some say he left and became a monk, styled Master Xue'an, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Some say he fled and became a monk known as Master Xue'an.

sentences.zh: 茅大芳，名誧，以字行，泰興人。博學能詩文。洪武中，為淮南學官，召對稱旨。擢秦府長史，制詞以董仲舒為言。大芳益奮激，盡心輔導。額其堂曰「希董」，方孝孺為之記。建文元年遷副都御史。燕師起，遺詩淮南守將梅殷，辭意激烈。聞者壯之。

translations.literal: Mao Dafang, personal name Pu, was known by his style. He was from Taixing. He was broadly learned and skilled in poetry and prose. During Hongwu he served as an educational official in Huainan; when summoned to respond, he satisfied the emperor's intent. He was promoted to chief secretary of the Qin princely establishment, and the imperial wording referred to Dong Zhongshu. Dafang became still more ardent and exerted himself fully in guidance. He inscribed his hall "Hoping for Dong," and Fang Xiaoru wrote the record for it. In Jianwen year one he was promoted to deputy censor-in-chief. When the Yan army rose, he sent a poem to Mei Yin, defender of Huainan, its words and meaning impassioned. Those who heard of it thought him heroic.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Dafang, whose personal name was Pu and who was known by his style, came from Taixing. Broadly learned and skilled in poetry and prose, he served under Hongwu as an educational official in Huainan. Summoned for an audience, he answered to the emperor's satisfaction and was promoted to chief secretary of the Qin princely establishment; the appointment text compared him to Dong Zhongshu. Dafang became still more stirred and devoted himself fully to guidance. He named his hall "Hoping for Dong," and Fang Xiaoru wrote the commemorative account. In Jianwen 1 he was promoted to deputy censor-in-chief. When the Yan army rose, he sent a poem to Mei Yin, defender of Huainan; its language was fierce and impassioned, and those who heard it praised his courage.

sentences.zh: 周璿，洪武末，以天策衛知事建言，擢左僉都御史。

translations.literal: Zhou Xuan, in late Hongwu, through his post as clerk of the Tiance Guard offered advice and was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xuan, in late Hongwu, offered counsel from his post in the Tiance Guard and was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 燕王稱帝，與大芳並見收，不屈死。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan declared himself emperor, he and Dafang were both seized and died unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan took the throne, he and Dafang were both arrested and died refusing to submit.

sentences.zh: 而大芳子順童、道壽俱論誅，二孫死獄中。

translations.literal: Dafang's sons Shuntong and Daoshou were both sentenced to execution; two grandsons died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Dafang's sons Shuntong and Daoshou were both condemned to death, and two grandsons died in prison.

sentences.zh: 卓敬，字惟恭，瑞安人。

translations.literal: Zhuo Jing, style Weigong, was a native of Ruian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo Jing, styled Weigong, came from Ruian.

sentences.zh: 穎悟過人，讀書十行俱下。

translations.literal: His quickness surpassed others; in reading he took in ten lines at once.
translations.idiomatic: Quick beyond his peers, he read ten lines at a glance.

sentences.zh: 舉洪武二十一年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-first year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-first year of Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 除戶科給事中，鯁直無所避。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supervising Secretary of the Household Section and was blunt and upright, sparing nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed supervising secretary of the household section, he was blunt and upright and spared no one.

sentences.zh: 時制度未備，諸王服乘擬天子。

translations.literal: At that time institutions were not complete; princes' dress and equipage rivaled the Son of Heaven's.
translations.idiomatic: Institutions were still incomplete, and princes dressed and traveled in a manner fit for the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 敬乘間言：「京師，天下視效。

translations.literal: Jing seized an occasion to say, "The capital is what the realm takes as its model.
translations.idiomatic: Jing seized an opportunity to say, "The capital is what the whole realm takes as its model.

sentences.zh: 陛下於諸王不早辨等威，而使服飾與太子埒，嫡庶相亂，尊卑無序，何以令天下？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty has not early distinguished ranks among the princes, yet lets their dress rival the crown prince's; legitimate and secondary lines are confused, honor and baseness lack order—how is the realm to be commanded?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has not early distinguished the princes' ranks, yet allows their dress to rival the crown prince's; legitimate and secondary lines are confused and honor and baseness lose order—how can you command the realm?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「爾言是，朕慮未及此。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Your words are right—I had not yet considered this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are right—I had not yet thought of this."

sentences.zh: 益器重之。

translations.literal: He valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: He valued Jing all the more highly.

sentences.zh: 他日與同官見，適八十一人，命改官為「元士」。

translations.literal: Another day, meeting with colleagues, there happened to be eighty-one men; he ordered their office title changed to "Primary Scholar."
translations.idiomatic: On another day, meeting with his colleagues, there happened to be eighty-one of them; the emperor ordered their title changed to "Primary Scholar."

sentences.zh: 尋以六科為政事本源，又改曰「源士」。

translations.literal: Soon, because the Six Sections were the root source of government affairs, he changed it again to "Source Scholar."
translations.idiomatic: Soon, because the six supervising-secretary sections were the root of government affairs, he changed the title again to "Source Scholar."

sentences.zh: 已，復稱給事中。

translations.literal: Later the title reverted to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Later the title reverted to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 歷官戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He rose in office to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 建文初，敬密疏言：「燕王智慮絕倫，雄才大略，酷類高帝。北平形勝地，士馬精強，金、元年由興。今宜徙封南昌，萬一有變，亦易控制。夫將萌而未動者，幾也；量時而可為者，勢也。勢非至剛莫能斷，幾非至明莫能察。」奏入，翌日召問。敬叩首曰：「臣所言天下至計，願陛下察之。」事竟寢。燕王即位，被執，責以建議徙燕，離間骨肉。敬厲聲曰：「惜先帝不用敬言耳！」帝怒，猶憐其才，命繫獄，使人諷以管仲、魏徵事。敬泣曰：「人臣委贄，有死無二。先皇帝曾無過舉，一旦橫行篡奪，恨不即死見故君地下，乃更欲臣我耶？」帝猶不忍殺。姚廣孝故與敬有隙，進曰：「敬言誠見用，上寧有今日。」乃斬之，誅其三族。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen, Jing secretly memorialized: "The Prince of Yan is unmatched in wisdom and planning, with heroic talent and broad strategy, and closely resembles the High Emperor. Beiping is a strategically advantageous place; its officers and horses are strong, and Jin and Yuan rose from it in former years. He should now be moved and enfeoffed at Nanchang; if by any chance there is a change, he will also be easier to control. That which is about to sprout but has not yet moved is opportunity; that which can be acted on by measuring the time is circumstance. Circumstance cannot be decided without utmost firmness, and opportunity cannot be perceived without utmost clarity." When the memorial was submitted, he was summoned and questioned the next day. Jing kowtowed and said, "What your servant has said is the greatest plan for the realm; may Your Majesty examine it." In the end the matter was shelved. When the Prince of Yan came to the throne, Jing was arrested and reproached for having proposed moving Yan and separating flesh and blood. Jing said in a stern voice, "I regret only that the former emperor did not use my words!" The emperor was angry, but still pitied his talent, ordered him imprisoned, and had someone hint to him with the precedents of Guan Zhong and Wei Zheng. Jing wept and said, "When a subject presents himself for service, there is death and no second loyalty. The late emperor had never made a mistaken act; then suddenly there was violent usurpation.
