I regret not dying at once to meet my former lord underground; and now you want me to serve you?" The emperor still could not bear to kill him. Yao Guangxiao had formerly had a rift with Jing and advanced, saying, "If Jing's words had truly been used, how could Your Majesty have today?" He was then beheaded, and his three clans were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianwen, Jing submitted a secret memorial: "The Prince of Yan is unequaled in intellect and planning, has heroic talent and grand strategy, and closely resembles the High Emperor. Beiping is a strong strategic position, with sturdy officers and horses; Jin and Yuan both rose from that region. He should now be moved to Nanchang. If anything happens, he will be easier to control. What is about to sprout but has not yet moved is opportunity; what can be acted on by measuring the time is circumstance. Circumstance cannot be decided without absolute firmness, and opportunity cannot be perceived without absolute clarity." After the memorial was submitted, Jing was summoned and questioned the next day. He kowtowed and said, "What I have stated is the supreme plan for the realm; may Your Majesty examine it." In the end the matter was shelved. When the Prince of Yan took the throne, Jing was arrested and reproached for proposing that Yan be moved, thereby separating close kin. Jing answered in a ringing voice, "My only regret is that the former emperor did not use my words!" The emperor was angry, yet still admired his talent, so he imprisoned him and had someone hint at the examples of Guan Zhong and Wei Zheng. Jing wept and said, "When a subject offers himself in service, there is death, not a second loyalty. The late emperor had committed no fault, and then suddenly came violent usurpation. I regret not dying at once to meet my old lord below; now you want me to serve you?" The emperor still could not bear to kill him. Yao Guangxiao, who had long had a rift with Jing, stepped forward and said, "If Jing's words had truly been used, how would Your Majesty have today?" Jing was then beheaded, and his three clans were executed.

sentences.zh: 敬立朝慷慨，美豐姿，善談論，凡天官、輿地、律歷、兵刑諸家，無不博究。

translations.literal: Jing was generous in court, handsome in bearing, skilled in discourse; whether astronomy, geography, calendrics, military law, or penal law—every school he broadly investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was forthright at court, handsome in bearing, and eloquent in debate; he had studied every field from astronomy and geography to calendrics, military law, and penal law.

sentences.zh: 成祖嘗嘆曰：：「國家養士三十年，惟得一卓敬。」

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor once sighed and said, "The state has nurtured scholars for thirty years and gained only one Zhuo Jing."
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor once sighed and said, "The state has nurtured scholars for thirty years and gained only one Zhuo Jing."

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，用御史屠叔方言，表墓建祠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli, on Censor Tu Shufang's proposal, his tomb was marked and a shrine built.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Wanli reign, on Censor Tu Shufang's proposal, a marked tomb and shrine were established for him.

sentences.zh: 同時戶部侍郎死者，有郭任、盧迥。

translations.literal: Vice Ministers of Revenue who died at the same time included Guo Ren and Lu Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Among the vice ministers of revenue who died at the same time were Guo Ren and Lu Jiong.

sentences.zh: 任，丹徒人，一曰定遠人。

translations.literal: Ren was a native of Dantu—or some say Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ren came from Dantu, though some say Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 廉慎有能。

translations.literal: He was incorrupt, cautious, and capable.
translations.idiomatic: He was honest, careful, and capable.

sentences.zh: 建文初，佐戶部。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen he assisted the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianwen he served in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 飲食起居俱在公署。

translations.literal: Food, drink, and daily living were all in the government offices.
translations.idiomatic: He ate, drank, and slept in the government offices.

sentences.zh: 時方貶削諸藩，任言：「天下事先本後末則易成。

translations.literal: When the feudatories were being degraded and reduced, Ren said, "In affairs of the realm, putting root before branch makes success easy.
translations.idiomatic: As the princely domains were being pared back, Ren said, "In governing the realm, put the root before the branches and success comes easily.

sentences.zh: 今日儲財粟，備軍實，果何為者？

translations.literal: Today we store wealth and grain and prepare military supplies—for what purpose, in the end?
translations.idiomatic: We are stockpiling wealth and grain and preparing armies—for what end?

sentences.zh: 乃北討周，南討湘。

translations.literal: Yet we campaign north against Zhou and south against Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yet we campaign north against Zhou and south against Xiang.

sentences.zh: 舍其本而末是圖，非策也。

translations.literal: Abandoning the root to pursue the branches is no strategy.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon the root and chase the branches is no strategy at all.

sentences.zh: 且兵貴神速，茍曠日持久，銳氣既竭，姑息隨之，將坐自困耳。」

translations.literal: Moreover, in warfare speed is prized; if days drag on, keen spirit is exhausted, indulgence follows, and one will sit trapped by one's own doing."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, war prizes speed; if the campaign drags on, sharp spirit fades, indulgence sets in, and we will trap ourselves."

sentences.zh: 燕王聞而惡之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan heard and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan heard this and hated him for it.

sentences.zh: 兵起，任與同官盧迥主調兵食。

translations.literal: When war rose, Ren together with his colleague Lu Jiong took charge of mobilizing troops and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out, Ren and his colleague Lu Jiong took charge of mobilizing troops and supplies.

sentences.zh: 京師失守被擒，不屈死之。

translations.literal: When the capital fell he was seized and died unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell he was captured and died refusing to submit.

sentences.zh: 子經亦論死，少子戍廣西。

translations.literal: His son Jing was also sentenced to death; his younger son was garrisoned in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing was likewise condemned to death; his younger son was banished to garrison service in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 迥，仙居人。

translations.literal: Jiong was a native of Xianju.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong came from Xianju.

sentences.zh: 爽朗不拘細行。

translations.literal: He was open and bright and unconstrained by small conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was open-hearted and cared little for petty proprieties.

sentences.zh: 喜飲酒，飲後輒高歌，人謂「迥狂」。

translations.literal: He loved wine; after drinking he would sing loudly, and people called him "Mad Jiong."
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and would sing loudly after drinking; people called him "Mad Jiong."

sentences.zh: 及仕，折節恭慎。

translations.literal: Once in office he restrained himself and was respectful and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he restrained himself and became respectful and careful.

sentences.zh: 建文三年，拜戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianwen he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianwen he was appointed vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 燕兵入，不屈。

translations.literal: When Yan troops entered he would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan forces entered the capital he refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 縛就刑，長謳而死。

translations.literal: Bound for execution, he sang long and died.
translations.idiomatic: Bound for execution, he sang at length as he died.

sentences.zh: 臺人祀之八忠祠。

translations.literal: The people of Taizhou sacrifice to him in the Shrine of the Eight Loyalists.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Taizhou honor him in the Shrine of the Eight Loyalists.

sentences.zh: 陳迪，字景道，宣城人。

translations.literal: Chen Di, style Jingdao, was a native of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Di, styled Jingdao, came from Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 祖宥賢，明初，從征有功，世撫州守禦百戶，因家焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Youxian, in early Ming, followed campaigns with merit and hereditarily held the post of garrison centurion at Fuzhou, settling his family there.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Youxian served in the founding campaigns with distinction and held a hereditary garrison post at Fuzhou, where the family settled.

sentences.zh: 迪倜儻有誌操。

translations.literal: Di was bold and free-spirited with resolute integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Di was bold and high-minded, with firm moral resolve.

sentences.zh: 辟府學訓導，為郡草《賀萬壽表》。

translations.literal: Recruited as instructor of the prefectural school, he drafted for the prefecture the "Memorial Congratulating Long Life."
translations.idiomatic: Recruited as prefectural school instructor, he drafted the county's "Memorial Congratulating Long Life."

sentences.zh: 太祖異之。

translations.literal: The founding emperor marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor was impressed.

sentences.zh: 久之，以通經薦，歷官侍講。

translations.literal: After long service he was recommended for mastery of the classics and rose to Reader.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was recommended for classical learning and rose to reader at court.

sentences.zh: 出為山東左參政，多惠政。

translations.literal: Sent out as Left Administrative Commissioner of Shandong, he enacted many benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as left administrative commissioner of Shandong, he left a record of benevolent governance.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 起復，除雲南右布政使。

translations.literal: Recalled from mourning, he was appointed Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning, he was appointed right provincial administration commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 普定、曲靖、烏撒、烏蒙諸蠻煽亂，迪率士兵擊破之，賜金幣。

translations.literal: The various tribes of Puding, Qujing, Wusa, and Wumeng stirred rebellion; Di led native troops to defeat them and was rewarded with gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes of Puding, Qujing, Wusa, and Wumeng rose in revolt, Di led local troops to defeat them and was rewarded with gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 建文初，征為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen he was summoned as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianwen he was summoned to serve as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時更修制度，沿革損益，迪議為多。

translations.literal: At that time institutions were being revised; in tracing origins, reducing, and adding, Di's proposals were many.
translations.idiomatic: As institutions were being revised, Di contributed many proposals on what to keep, cut, or add.

sentences.zh: 會以水旱詔百官集議，迪請清刑獄，招流民，凡二十余事，皆從之。

translations.literal: When flood and drought led to an edict summoning officials for joint deliberation, Di requested clearing the prisons, recruiting displaced people, and more than twenty matters in all—all were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: When flood and drought prompted the emperor to summon officials for counsel, Di proposed clearing the prisons, resettling refugees, and more than twenty other measures—all were adopted.

sentences.zh: 尋加太子少保。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 李景隆等數戰敗，迪陳大計。

translations.literal: When Li Jinglong and others suffered repeated defeats, Di set forth the grand strategy.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Jinglong's repeated defeats, Di laid out a grand strategy.

sentences.zh: 命督運軍儲。

translations.literal: He was ordered to supervise transport of military stores.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to supervise the transport of military supplies.

sentences.zh: 已，聞變，趨赴京師。

translations.literal: Later, hearing of the crisis, he hurried to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later, hearing of the crisis, he rushed to the capital.

sentences.zh: 燕王即帝位，召迪責問，抗聲不屈。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan took the throne he summoned Di to rebuke and question him; Di answered defiantly and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan took the throne he summoned Di to account for himself; Di answered defiantly and would not submit.

sentences.zh: 命與子鳳山、丹山等六人磔於市。

translations.literal: He ordered Di together with his sons Fengshan and Danshan and six others in all torn apart in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Di, together with his sons Fengshan and Danshan and four others, torn apart in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 既死，人於衣帶中得詩及《五噫歌》，辭意悲烈。

translations.literal: After death, people found in his belt poems and the "Five Sighs Song," their words tragic and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, poems and the "Five Sighs Song" were found in his belt—words of tragic defiance.

sentences.zh: 蒼頭侯來保拾其遺骸歸葬。

translations.literal: His servant Hou Laibao gathered his remains and returned them for burial.
translations.idiomatic: His servant Hou Laibao gathered his remains and buried them.

sentences.zh: 妻管縊死。

translations.literal: His wife Guan hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Guan hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 幼子珠生五月，乳母潛置溝中，得免。

translations.literal: His infant son Zhu, five months old, was secretly placed in a ditch by his wet nurse and escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: His infant son Zhu, only five months old, was secretly left in a ditch by his wet nurse and survived.

sentences.zh: 八歲，為怨家所訐。

translations.literal: At eight years old he was denounced by an enemy family.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he was denounced by an enemy family.

sentences.zh: 成祖宥其死，戍撫寧。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor spared his life and exiled him to garrison at Funing.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor spared his life and banished him to Funing.

sentences.zh: 尋徙登州，為蓬萊人。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Dengzhou and became a native of Penglai.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to Dengzhou and became a man of Penglai.

sentences.zh: 洪熙初，赦還鄉，給田產。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongxi he was pardoned and returned home; fields and property were granted.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Hongxi he was pardoned and sent home with fields and property granted.

sentences.zh: 成化中，寧國知府塗觀建祠祀迪。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua reign the prefect of Ningguo, Tu Guan, built a shrine to sacrifice to Di.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chenghua reign Prefect Tu Guan of Ningguo built a shrine to honor Di.

sentences.zh: 弘治間，裔孫鼎舉進士，仕至應天府尹，剛鯁有聲。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi reign his descendant Ding passed the jinshi examination, served to Intendant of Yingtian Prefecture, and was famed for stern integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongzhi reign his descendant Ding passed the jinshi and rose to intendant of Yingtian Prefecture, famed for stern integrity.

sentences.zh: 黃魁，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Huang Kui—his origin is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Kui's place of origin is unknown.

sentences.zh: 為禮部侍郎，有學行，習典禮。

translations.literal: He was Vice Minister of Rites, possessed learning and conduct, and was versed in ceremonial regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice minister of rites, was learned and upright, and versed in ceremonial law.

sentences.zh: 迪及侍郎黃觀皆愛敬人。

translations.literal: Di and Vice Minister Huang Guan were both loved and respected by people.
translations.idiomatic: Both Di and Vice Minister Huang Guan were widely loved and respected.

sentences.zh: 燕兵入，不屈死。

translations.literal: When Yan troops entered he died unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan forces entered the capital he died refusing to submit.

sentences.zh: 有巨敬者，平涼人。

translations.literal: There was Ju Jing, a native of Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Ju Jing, from Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 為御史，改戶部主事，充史官，以清慎稱。

translations.literal: He was a censor, transferred to a principal clerk post in the Ministry of Revenue, served as historiographer, and was known for purity and caution.
translations.idiomatic: A censor, then a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue and a historiographer, he was known for integrity and care.

sentences.zh: 與迪同不屈死，夷其族。

translations.literal: Like Di he died unyielding; his clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Like Di he died refusing to submit, and his clan was exterminated.

sentences.zh: 景清，本耿姓，訛景，真寧人。

translations.literal: Jing Qing was originally surnamed Geng; the character was corrupted to Jing; he was a native of Zhenning.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Qing was originally surnamed Geng—the character was corrupted to Jing—and he came from Zhenning.

sentences.zh: 倜儻尚大節，讀書一過不忘。

translations.literal: Bold and free-spirited, he prized great integrity; in reading, once over he did not forget.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and high-minded, he prized great integrity and never forgot what he read at a single pass.

sentences.zh: 洪武中進士，授編修，改御史。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the Hongwu reign, he was appointed Compiler and transferred to Censor.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi under Hongwu, he became a compiler and then a censor.

sentences.zh: 三十年春，召見，命署左僉都御史。

translations.literal: In spring of the thirtieth year he was summoned for audience and ordered to act as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirtieth year he was summoned to court and appointed acting Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 以奏疏字誤，懷印更改，為給事中所劾，下詔獄。

translations.literal: Because of a wrong character in a memorial he carried his seal to make corrections and was impeached by a supervising secretary and cast into the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: When a memorial contained a wrong character he carried his seal to correct it, was impeached by a supervising secretary, and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 尋宥之。

translations.literal: Soon he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon pardoned.

sentences.zh: 詔巡察川、陜私茶，除金華知府。

translations.literal: By edict he inspected private tea in Sichuan and Shaanxi and was appointed Prefect of Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he inspected illicit tea trade in Sichuan and Shaanxi, then was appointed prefect of Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 建文初，為北平參議。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen he was a councilor in Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianwen he served as a councilor in Beiping.

sentences.zh: 燕王與語，言論明晰，大稱賞。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan conversed with him; his discourse was clear and he was greatly praised.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan spoke with him, found his discourse lucid, and praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 再遷御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 燕師入，諸臣死者甚眾。

translations.literal: When the Yan army entered, many court officials died.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan forces entered the capital, many officials died.

sentences.zh: 清素預密謀，且約孝孺等同殉國，至是獨詣闕自歸，成祖命仍其官，委蛇班行者久之。

translations.literal: Qing had long been privy to secret plots and had even agreed with Xiaoru and others to die for the state together; now he alone went to the palace to surrender himself. The Yongle Emperor ordered him kept in his office and for a long time he went through the motions in court procession.
translations.idiomatic: Qing had taken part in secret plots and had even agreed with Xiaoru and others to die for the state; now he alone presented himself at court to surrender. The Yongle Emperor kept him in office, and for a long time he went through the motions at court.

sentences.zh: 一日早朝，清衣緋懷刃入。

translations.literal: One day at the dawn audience Qing wore scarlet robes and entered with a blade hidden on his person.
translations.idiomatic: One morning at court Qing entered in scarlet robes with a blade hidden on his person.

sentences.zh: 先是，日者奏異星赤色犯帝座，甚急。

translations.literal: Earlier, the calendar officer reported an unusual star of red color encroaching on the imperial throne—a very urgent omen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the calendar officer had reported a red aberrant star encroaching on the imperial throne—a dire omen.

sentences.zh: 成祖故疑清。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor had therefore already suspected Qing.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor had therefore already suspected Qing.

sentences.zh: 及朝，清獨著緋。

translations.literal: At court Qing alone wore scarlet.
translations.idiomatic: At court Qing alone wore scarlet.

sentences.zh: 命搜之，得所藏刃。

translations.literal: He was ordered searched and the hidden blade was found.
translations.idiomatic: He was searched and the hidden blade was found.

sentences.zh: 詰責，清奮起曰：「欲為故主報仇耳！」

translations.literal: Rebuked and questioned, Qing roused himself and said, "I wished only to avenge my former lord!"
translations.idiomatic: Under interrogation Qing cried out, "I meant only to avenge my former lord!"

sentences.zh: 成祖怒，磔死，族之。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor was enraged; he was torn apart by execution and his clan exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor flew into a rage; Qing was torn apart by execution and his clan exterminated.

sentences.zh: 籍其鄉，轉相攀染，謂之「瓜蔓抄」，村裏為墟。

translations.literal: His home district was registered and implicated in succession—called "melon-vine confiscation"—and villages were reduced to ruins.
translations.idiomatic: His home district was registered and guilt spread from house to house in what was called "melon-vine confiscation," until villages lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 初，金川門之啟，御史連楹叩馬欲刺成祖，被殺，屍植立不仆。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Jinchuan Gate was opened, Censor Lian Ying seized the prince's horse and tried to stab the Yongle Emperor; he was killed, and his corpse stood planted upright without falling.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jinchuan Gate was opened, Censor Lian Ying seized the prince's horse and tried to stab the Yongle Emperor; he was killed, and his corpse stood upright without falling.

sentences.zh: 楹，襄垣人。

translations.literal: Ying was a native of Xiangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ying came from Xiangyuan.

sentences.zh: 胡閏，字松友，鄱陽人。

translations.literal: Hu Run, style Songyou, was a native of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Run, styled Songyou, came from Poyang.

sentences.zh: 太祖征陳友諒，過長沙王吳芮祠，見題壁詩，奇之，立召見帳前。

translations.literal: When the founding emperor campaigned against Chen Youliang, passing the shrine of King Wu Rui of Changsha he saw a poem inscribed on the wall, marveled at it, and immediately summoned the author before his tent.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Chen Youliang, the founding emperor passed the shrine of King Wu Rui of Changsha, saw a poem on the wall, marveled at it, and summoned the author to his tent at once.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年，郡舉秀才，入見。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu the prefecture presented him as xiucai and he had audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Hongwu the prefecture presented him as a xiucai scholar and he was received at court.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此書生故題詩鄱陽廟壁者邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Is this not the scholar who once inscribed a poem on the wall of the Poyang shrine?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Is this not the scholar who wrote on the wall of the Poyang shrine?"

sentences.zh: 授都督府都事，遷經歷。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk of the Chief Military Commission and transferred to Registrar.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief clerk of the chief military commission and later promoted to registrar.

sentences.zh: 建文初，選右補闕，尋進大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen he was selected as Right Remonstrating Censor and soon promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianwen he was made Right Remonstrating Censor and soon promoted to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 燕師起，與齊、黃輩晝夜畫軍事。

translations.literal: When the Yan army rose he with Qi, Huang, and their circle plotted military affairs day and night.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army rose he joined Qi, Huang, and their circle in planning military affairs day and night.

sentences.zh: 京師陷，召閏，不屈，與子傳道俱死。

translations.literal: When the capital fell he was summoned; he would not yield and died together with his son Chuandao.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell he was summoned, refused to submit, and died together with his son Chuandao.

sentences.zh: 幼子傳慶戍邊。

translations.literal: His younger son Chuanqing was exiled to frontier garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Chuanqing was banished to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 四歲女郡奴入功臣家，稍長識大義，日以爨灰汙面。

translations.literal: His four-year-old daughter Junu entered a meritorious minister's household; when she grew somewhat older she understood great principle and daily smeared her face with hearth ash.
translations.idiomatic: His four-year-old daughter Junu was taken into a meritorious minister's household; as she grew she understood what loyalty meant and daily smeared her face with hearth ash.

sentences.zh: 洪熙初，赦還鄉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongxi she was pardoned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Hongxi she was pardoned and sent home.

sentences.zh: 貧甚，誓不嫁。

translations.literal: Deeply poor, she vowed never to marry.
translations.idiomatic: Utterly poor, she vowed never to marry.

sentences.zh: 見者競遺以錢谷，曰：「此忠臣女也。」

translations.literal: Those who saw her vied to give money and grain, saying, "This is a loyal minister's daughter."
translations.idiomatic: Those who saw her pressed money and grain on her, saying, "This is a loyal minister's daughter."

sentences.zh: 高翔，朝邑人。

translations.literal: Gao Xiang was a native of Chaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xiang came from Chaoyi.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，以明經為監察御史。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu reign, through the classics examination he became Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu he entered office through the classics examination and became an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 建文時，戮力兵事。

translations.literal: In the Jianwen reign he exerted all strength in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianwen he threw himself into military affairs.

sentences.zh: 成祖聞其名，與閏同召，欲用之。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor heard his name and summoned him together with Run, wishing to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor heard his name and summoned him with Run, intending to employ him.

sentences.zh: 翔喪服入見，語不遜。

translations.literal: Xiang entered audience in mourning garb; his words were not deferential.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang came before the throne in mourning dress and spoke without deference.

sentences.zh: 族之，發其先冢，親黨悉戍邊。

translations.literal: His clan was exterminated; his ancestors' tombs were opened; kin and associates were all exiled to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was exterminated, his ancestors' tombs desecrated, and all his kin banished to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 諸給高氏產者皆加稅，曰：「令世世罵翔也。」

translations.literal: All who were granted Gao clan property had extra tax imposed, with the words, "Let them curse Xiang generation after generation."
translations.idiomatic: All who received Gao family property were taxed extra, with the order, "Let them curse Xiang for generations."

sentences.zh: 王度，字子中，歸善人。

translations.literal: Wang Du, style Zizhong, was a native of Guishan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Du, styled Zizhong, came from Guishan.

sentences.zh: 少力學，工文辭，用明經薦為山東道監察御史。

translations.literal: In youth he studied strenuously and was skilled in literary composition; through the classics examination he was recommended as Investigating Censor of the Shandong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied hard and wrote well; recommended through the classics examination, he became investigating censor of the Shandong circuit.

sentences.zh: 建文時，燕兵起，度悉心贊畫。

translations.literal: In the Jianwen reign, when the Yan army rose, Du devoted himself to planning and counsel.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianwen, when the Yan army rose, Du threw himself into planning and counsel.

sentences.zh: 及王師屢敗，度奏請募兵。

translations.literal: When the imperial army suffered repeated defeats, Du memorialized requesting recruitment of troops.
translations.idiomatic: After the imperial armies suffered repeated defeats, Du memorialized asking to raise new troops.

sentences.zh: 小河之捷，奉命勞軍徐州。

translations.literal: After the victory at Xiaohe, he was ordered on commission to comfort the army at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory at Xiaohe he was ordered to visit the army at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 還，方孝孺與度書，誓死社稷。

translations.literal: On his return, Fang Xiaoru wrote to Du, vowing to die for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Fang Xiaoru wrote to Du, swearing to die with the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 燕王稱帝，坐方黨謫戍賀縣，又坐語不遜，族。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan declared himself emperor, Du was punished as a member of Fang's faction and exiled to garrison at Hexian; later for disrespectful words his clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan took the throne, Du was punished as a member of Fang's faction and banished to Hexian; later, for disrespectful speech, his clan was exterminated.

sentences.zh: 度有智計。

translations.literal: Du possessed resourceful stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Du was shrewd and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 盛庸之代景隆，度密陳便宜，是以有東昌之捷。

translations.literal: When Sheng Yong replaced Jinglong, Du secretly set forth advantageous plans, and for this reason there was the victory at Dongchang.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng Yong replaced Jinglong, Du secretly proposed the strategy that won the victory at Dongchang.

sentences.zh: 景隆征還，赦不誅，反用事。

translations.literal: Jinglong was recalled from campaign, pardoned from execution, and instead wielded power.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglong was recalled, spared execution, and returned to power instead.

sentences.zh: 忌庸等功，讒間之，度亦見疏。

translations.literal: Jealous of Yong and others' merit, he slandered and estranged them; Du too was distanced.
translations.idiomatic: Jealous of Yong and the others' achievements, he slandered them and drove them apart; Du too fell from favor.

sentences.zh: 論者以其用有未盡，惜之。

translations.literal: Commentators, because his employment was not fully exhausted, regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Later commentators regretted that his talents were never fully used.

sentences.zh: 戴德彜，奉化人。

translations.literal: Dai Deyi was a native of Fenghua.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Deyi came from Fenghua.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十七年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-seventh year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-seventh year of Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 累官侍講。

translations.literal: He rose in office to Reader.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to reader at court.

sentences.zh: 太祖諭之曰：「翰林雖職文學，然既列禁近，凡國家政治得失，民生利害，當知無不言。

translations.literal: The founding emperor instructed him: "Though the Hanlin Academy is charged with letters, once you stand within the forbidden precincts, on every gain or loss in state governance and every harm or benefit to the people's livelihood, you should speak without holding back.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor told him: "Though the Hanlin Academy is a literary office, once you stand within the forbidden precincts you must speak without reserve on every gain or loss in government and every harm or benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 昔唐陸贄、崔群、李絳在翰林，皆能正言讜論，補益當時。

translations.literal: In old times Tang's Lu Zhi, Cui Qun, and Li Jiang in the Hanlin all could speak uprightly with forthright counsel and benefit their age.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang times Lu Zhi, Cui Qun, and Li Jiang in the Hanlin all spoke boldly and gave forthright counsel that benefited their age.

sentences.zh: 汝宜以古人自期。」

translations.literal: You ought to take the ancients as your measure."
translations.idiomatic: You should hold yourself to that standard."

sentences.zh: 已，改監察御史。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 建文時，改左拾遺。

translations.literal: In the Jianwen reign he was changed to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianwen he was made Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 燕王入，召見，不屈，死之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan entered he was summoned for audience, would not yield, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan entered the capital he was summoned, refused to submit, and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 德彜死時，兄弟並從京師。

translations.literal: When Deyi died his brothers were all in the capital with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Deyi died his brothers were all with him in the capital.

sentences.zh: 嫂項家居，聞變，度禍且族，令闔舍逃去。

translations.literal: His sister-in-law Xiang remained at home; hearing of the crisis, she judged disaster would reach the clan and ordered the whole household to flee.
translations.idiomatic: His sister-in-law Xiang was at home; hearing of the crisis, she judged the clan would be wiped out and ordered the whole household to flee.

sentences.zh: 匿德彜二子山中，毀戴氏族譜，獨身留家。

translations.literal: She hid Deyi's two sons in the mountains, destroyed the Dai clan genealogy, and alone remained at home.
translations.idiomatic: She hid Deyi's two sons in the mountains, destroyed the Dai clan genealogy, and stayed home alone.

sentences.zh: 收者至，無所得，械項至京，搒掠終無一言，戴族獲全。

translations.literal: When arresters came they gained nothing; Xiang was shackled and taken to the capital, beaten and tortured yet never spoke a word, and the Dai clan was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: When arresters came they found nothing; Xiang was shackled and taken to the capital, tortured without uttering a word, and the Dai clan was spared.

sentences.zh: 時御史不屈死者，有諸城謝升、聊城丁誌方。

translations.literal: Among censors who died unyielding at that time were Xie Sheng of Zhucheng and Ding Zhifang of Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Among the censors who died refusing to submit were Xie Sheng of Zhucheng and Ding Zhifang of Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 而懷寧甘霖從容就戮，子孫相戒不復仕。

translations.literal: Gan Lin of Huaining went calmly to execution; descendants warned one another never to take office again.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Lin of Huaining went calmly to his execution; his descendants warned one another never to serve in office again.

sentences.zh: 又董鏞，不知何許人。

translations.literal: There was also Dong Yong—his origin is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Dong Yong, whose place of origin is unknown.

sentences.zh: 諸御史有誌節者，時時會鏞所，誓以死報國。

translations.literal: Censors of resolute integrity would from time to time meet at Yong's place and swear to die for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Censors of firm resolve would gather at Yong's home and swear to die for the realm.

sentences.zh: 諸將校觀望不力戰，鏞輒露章劾之。

translations.literal: When commanders and officers looked on without fighting hard, Yong would expose memorials impeaching them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever officers held back and fought half-heartedly, Yong would submit open memorials impeaching them.

sentences.zh: 城破被殺，家戍極邊。

translations.literal: When the city fell he was killed; his family was garrisoned on the farthest frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he was killed, and his family was banished to the farthest frontier.

sentences.zh: 而給事中死者，則有陳繼之、韓永、葉福三人。

translations.literal: Among supervising secretaries who died were three: Chen Jizhi, Han Yong, and Ye Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Among the supervising secretaries who died were Chen Jizhi, Han Yong, and Ye Fu.

sentences.zh: 繼之，莆田人，建文二年進士。

translations.literal: Jizhi was a native of Putian and passed the jinshi in the second year of Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi came from Putian and passed the jinshi in the second year of Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 時江南僧道多腴田，繼之請人限五畝，余以賦民。

translations.literal: At that time monks and Daoists in Jiangnan held much fertile land; Jizhi requested that each person be limited to five mu and the remainder taxed to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Monks and Daoists in the lower Yangzi region held much fertile land; Jizhi proposed limiting each to five mu and taxing the rest to the people.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 兵事亟，數條奏機宜。

translations.literal: Military affairs were urgent; he repeatedly memorialized on timely measures.
translations.idiomatic: As war grew urgent he submitted repeated memorials on strategy.

sentences.zh: 燕兵入，不屈，見殺，父母兄弟悉戍邊。

translations.literal: When Yan troops entered he would not yield, was killed, and parents and brothers were all exiled to frontier garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan forces entered he refused to submit and was killed; his parents and brothers were all banished to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 永，西安人，或曰浮山。

translations.literal: Yong was a native of Xi'an—or some say Fushan.
translations.idiomatic: Yong came from Xi'an, though some say Fushan.

sentences.zh: 貌魁梧，音吐洪亮，每慷慨論兵事。

translations.literal: His appearance was imposing, his voice resonant; he often spoke passionately on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Imposing in bearing and resonant in speech, he often spoke passionately about military affairs.

sentences.zh: 燕王入，欲官之，抗辭，不屈死。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan entered he wished to give him office; Yong answered defiantly and died unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan entered he offered Yong office; Yong answered defiantly and died refusing to submit.

sentences.zh: 福，侯官人，繼之同年生。

translations.literal: Fu was a native of Houguan and a classmate of Jizhi in the same year.
translations.idiomatic: Fu came from Houguan and had passed the examinations in the same year as Jizhi.

sentences.zh: 燕兵至，守金川門，城陷，死之。

translations.literal: When Yan troops arrived he defended the Jinchuan Gate; when the city fell he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan forces arrived he defended the Jinchuan Gate and died when the city fell.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：帝王成事，蓋由天授。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The accomplishment of emperors and kings is granted by Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: The triumph of emperors and kings is granted by Heaven.

sentences.zh: 成祖之得天下，非人力所能禦也。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor's gaining of the realm was not something human strength could withstand.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor's seizure of the realm was not something human strength could have withstood.

sentences.zh: 齊、黃、方、練之儔，抱謀國之忠，而乏制勝之策。

translations.literal: Men such as Qi, Huang, Fang, and Lian embraced loyalty in plotting for the state yet lacked strategies to secure victory.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Qi, Huang, Fang, and Lian were loyal in their counsel for the state yet lacked the strategies to win.

sentences.zh: 然其忠憤激發，視刀鋸鼎鑊甘之若飴，百世而下，凜凜猶有生氣。

translations.literal: Yet their loyal rage was roused; they regarded blade, saw, cauldron, and boiling cauldron as sweet as candy—a hundred generations hence they still seem vividly alive.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their loyal fury was roused; they faced blade, saw, and cauldron as gladly as sweets—and a hundred generations later they still seem vividly alive.

sentences.zh: 是豈泄然不恤國事而以一死自謝者所可同日道哉！

translations.literal: How can this be spoken of in the same breath as those who listlessly cared nothing for state affairs and used a single death to excuse themselves!
translations.idiomatic: Surely they cannot be spoken of in the same breath as those who cared nothing for the realm and offered only a single death in excuse!

sentences.zh: 由是觀之，固未可以成敗之常見論也。

translations.literal: Viewed thus, one truly cannot judge them by the common measure of success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, they cannot be judged by the common measure of success and failure alone.
